title: Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
abstract: Women are a vulnerable population for mental illnesses, with the perinatal period representing a particularly high-risk susceptible window. Whereas maternal mental health research often narrowly focused on postpartum depression, psychological disturbances during pregnancy received insufficient attention. Here we analyzed a Chinese nationwide 13-year maternity cohort involving 216,442 pregnant women, revealing that the prevalence of prenatal mental distress symptoms peaked at 31.8%. We identified a broad spectrum of risk determinants, spanning socioeconomic disadvantages, behavioral vulnerabilities, medical histories and suboptimal residential environmental exposures. We estimated that 1.61 (95% uncertainty interval: 1.35–1.88) million prenatal mental distress symptoms were attributable to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and heatwave exposure, while green spaces prevented 791.7 (95% uncertainty interval: 648.1–948.9) thousand cases. We further delineated multiple pathways through which urban greening confers mental well-being benefits, including attenuation of pollution-associated stress, reduction of heatwave occurrence, encouragement of outdoor physical activity and intrinsic mental restoration. Our study ultimately provides policy-oriented evidence to inform fertility-supportive and health-promoting urban planning, echoing China’s ‘three-child policy’ and ‘Healthy China 2030’ blueprint. In a cohort of 216,000+ pregnant women across China, air pollution and heat were linked to higher risks of prenatal mental distress, while nearby green space was protective. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities.

title: Thermochemical adsorption at high overpotentials limits molecular CO-to-methanol electroreduction
abstract: Electrocatalysis modulates interfacial charge-transfer kinetics through potential control. However, it remains unclear how thermochemical steps, such as adsorption, dictate these overall kinetics. Here we determine CO-reduction limiting currents by measuring CO-oxidation limiting currents, allowing mass-transport effects to be deconvoluted from the CO-reduction kinetics. Using CO-to-methanol conversion on molecular catalysts as a model system, we show that while the reaction rate is limited by an electrochemical step at low overpotentials, the thermochemical CO adsorption step becomes rate limiting at high overpotentials. Cation-dependent variations in CO adsorption energies and activation energies align with the Brønsted-Evans-Polanyi principle, establishing CO adsorption energy as a robust kinetic descriptor. We further demonstrate that cobalt phthalocyanine supported on carbon nanotubes enables appreciable CO-to-methanol conversion due to its enhanced CO adsorption compared to other metal phthalocyanines. Ultimately, these findings illuminate an inherent thermochemical constraint on electrolysis and provide a kinetic framework to identify when such limitations become rate determining.

title: Disentanglement of interfacial electric fields and electrochemical potential gradients reveals a multidimensional kinetic landscape
abstract:
Abstract
                  Electrochemical reactions occur at solid–liquid interfaces, where the applied electrochemical potential gradient can act as thermodynamic driving force but can also induce interfacial polarization. A key question has long been how local changes in the chemical potentials of the electrons and the associated excess charge and electric fields impact catalyst kinetics. Here we combine temperature-dependent current transients from oxidative CO stripping with a CO coverage-dependent potential of zero total charge and Raman spectroscopy. We observe a reduction of the activation energy with increasing driving force. By contrast, increasing the distance between the applied potential and the potential of zero total charge results in an increase in the apparent activation energy, which we ascribe to an electric field effect in the double layer. More generally, the results demonstrate how interfacial changes in the chemical potentials give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape, in which single-descriptor kinetics fail to capture the nature of the overpotential.

title: Breaking symmetry in nanoparticle superlattices via spontaneous valency
abstract: Nanoparticle superlattices enable programmable material structure through ligand-mediated interactions, but attractive ligand interactions typically limit assembly to densely packed lattices that maximize nearest-neighbour bonding. Intentionally programmed directional bonding and valency are therefore typically assumed to require particle-level anisotropy in shape or surface patterning. Here, using assemblies of flexible, electrostatically active isotropic nanoparticles, we show that valency need not be encoded by particle geometry, but can instead emerge spontaneously during assembly. When ligand coronas are sufficiently deformable, ligands reconfigure to align along interparticle interfaces, generating an effective valency. Using a combination of experiment and simulation, we show that increasing ligand deformability lowers lattice coordination numbers, and identify design considerations for assembling isotropic building blocks into lattices with lower coordination, packing density and symmetry than would be predicted from hard-sphere packing. The work presented here therefore establishes ligand flexibility as a design parameter for programming coordination in nanoparticle assembly.

title: Spin currents in polariton waveguides driven by bright and dark excitons
abstract: The optical spin Hall effect enables the spatial separation of four domains of circularly polarized light from a linearly polarized source through photonic spin-orbit coupling, which arises from non-degenerate transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic modes. This mechanism is ineffective for incoherent photoluminescence. In transition metal dichalcogenide monolayers, bright excitons possess in-plane electric dipoles and strong oscillator strengths, whereas dark excitons have out-of-plane dipoles. Here, by embedding WS2 monolayers in waveguide microcavities, we demonstrate strong coupling between bright excitons and photonic modes, forming exciton-polaritons. Under non-resonant pumping, dark excitons become strongly populated and feed both transverse-magnetic- and transverse-electric-like exciton-polariton modes, each with an out-of-plane electric-field component. We observe the optical spin Hall effect in waveguide polaritons, leading to the formation of eight polarization domains and spin-polarized polariton currents propagating up to 92 ± 1 μm at room temperature. These results establish transition metal dichalcogenide-based polaritonic waveguides as a promising platform for room-temperature spin-optoelectronic devices.

title: Set efficiency criteria for access to geological carbon dioxide storage
abstract: Geological CO2 storage sites are critical to achieving climate-relevant carbon sequestration. Efficiency metrics should be used to ensure that limited storage capacity is not used on CO2 from capture projects with high levels of life-cycle carbon emissions.

abstract: Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. title: Directing solvent reactivity
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.

title: Trifunctional zirconium catalysis-enabled triple modular synthesis
abstract: While zirconium catalysis has been predominantly confined to Lewis acid and redox applications in homogeneous synthesis, its potential in photocatalysis—particularly in C–H activation—remains largely unexplored. Here, with the demonstration of photoinduced inner-sphere α-homolysis (ligand-to-metal charge transfer) in zirconium catalysis, we report a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system synergistically integrating photochemical, Lewis acid and redox catalysis for triple modular synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles, rendering structurally diverse benzylamines (up to 98% yield) and their deuterated analogues under mild conditions. Mechanistic studies validate a multifunctional catalytic cycle combining ligand-to-metal charge transfer-initiated radical chemistry with a ZrIV-mediated carbocation pathway. The protocol’s synthetic power is showcased through late-stage diversification of bioactive compounds, streamlined drug analogue synthesis, direct valorization of gaseous alkanes and gram-scale production with 100% atom economy. Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. Now trifunctional zirconium catalysis enables modular benzylamine synthesis from alkanes, aldehydes and nitriles by integrating photochemical, redox and Lewis acid reactivity.

title: Optimizing systems rather than parts
abstract: Developing and deploying clean technologies to reach net-zero carbon emissions will require more than optimizing individual processes and technologies. System-level thinking is needed to identify trade-offs, handle uncertainty and future scenarios, and support decision-making, as highlighted by articles in a new Collection.

title: Secondary materials in photovoltaics manufacturing
abstract: The use of secondary materials in photovoltaics could reduce resource demand, waste generation and supply-chain risks. This Review benchmarks recycled content use across silicon photovoltaic materials and identifies technical and market barriers to wider adoption.

title: Stable anode-free sodium batteries enabled by controlled oligomerization
abstract: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. Here the authors introduce a moderate-strain cyclic ether that redirects electrolyte decomposition to form a thin, robust interphase, thereby minimizing sodium consumption and extending cycling stability.

title: Southeast Asian voices on climate change
abstract: Responding to the increasing risks of climate change in Southeast Asia requires research and effective action that considers the unique challenges of the region. In this Viewpoint, researchers and practitioners from the region share their views on the progress made in understanding and responding to climate change.

abstract: The protein sequence space is incredibly vast and identifying functional variants is like finding a needle in a haystack. In 1997, Boder and Wittrup developed a method to display proteins on the surface of yeast, unlocking the ability to screen large libraries of mutants to identify proteins with desired characteristics.

abstract: Baseline construction shapes estimates of mitigation cost, ambition and progress, while no-policy counterfactuals could vary with choices about policy, technology and development. Rather than relying on one constructed baseline, assessments and related conclusions should be compared across plausible baselines.

title: Wild–urban gradient leads to ecological stratification in Singapore’s long-tailed macaques
abstract: Large-scale urbanization, with a mosaic of different disturbance levels, forces species to adapt in often unpredictable ways. To better understand such adaptations, we here use a multidimensional analysis of DNA from >350 fecal samples of long-tailed macaques (Macaca fascicularis) collected across a wild–urban gradient in highly urbanized Singapore, investigating their population structure, diet and microbiome. Macaques grouped into eight distinct matrilines, which exhibited specific habitat associations. Total plants in the diet were more diverse in wild than urban areas, with the total diversity of an important group of exotic fruiting plants decreasing markedly along the wild–urban gradient. Similarly, total bacterial diversity, including that of pathogens, showed steep declines from wild to urban habitat. Our analysis suggests that the wild–urban gradient produces different pathogenic and dietary environments and that kinship and learning may lead to adaptations to a diverse city landscape. These results open avenues for understanding animal adjustment to anthropogenic environments in general and specifically enable managers and city planners to take into account long-tailed macaques’ relationships, habitat-use patterns and dietary preferences to facilitate human–macaque coexistence. This study assessed the diet, gut bacteria and habitat preferences of long-tailed macaques in Singapore across a gradient of urbanization. Animal dietary diversity and gut bacterial diversity both declined with urbanization, while dietary plant diversity varied with urbanization according to ecological category. The macaque population exhibits eight female-line groups associated with specific habitats ranging in degree of urbanicity.

title: Brazil’s data-driven plan for climate-resilient healthcare

title: Rational design of lipid nanoparticles for brain delivery of RNA therapeutics
abstract: Effective delivery of RNA therapeutics to the brain remains challenging due to the multiple barriers of the central nervous system (CNS). To probe molecular scaffolds that could help overcome these barriers, we analysed the pharmaceutical profiles of over 100 CNS-active drugs and identified hydroxyzine (HX) as a promising scaffold for designing ionizable lipids with improved brain-targeting properties. Specifically, HX1 liquid nanoparticles (LNPs) achieved robust mRNA delivery to the brain through multiple trafficking pathways across CNS barriers. HX1 LNPs also enabled efficient gene editing in mouse brains via co-delivery of CRISPR mRNA and guide RNA and effectively delivered luciferase mRNA to the brain of a non-human primate. Moreover, HX1 LNPs carrying Il10 mRNA mitigated radiation-induced brain injury in mice, highlighting their potential for preventive treatment in the presence of intact CNS barriers. These findings establish HX1 LNPs as a promising translational platform for delivering therapeutic mRNAs and genome-editing components to the brain.

title: Three-dimensional imaging of individual carbon atoms
abstract: Ptychography is a computational microscopy method that unifies crystallography and microscopy by combining coherent diffraction with iterative phase retrieval. Although multislice electron ptychography achieves deep-sub-ångström lateral resolution, its depth resolution is typically at the nanometre scale. Ptychographic atomic electron tomography (pAET) has enabled three-dimensional (3D) atomic structure determination in nanomaterials, yet reliably resolving individual light atoms remains challenging. Here, using twisted bilayer graphene as a model moiré system, we demonstrate pAET for 3D localization of 6,648 carbon atoms with a precision of 0.12 Å. The resulting 3D atomic structure reveals stacking-dependent interlayer spacing and corrugation across the moiré supercell, as well as chiral lattice distortions with meron-like, anti-meron-like and anti-skyrmion-like textures. Density functional theory calculations based on the experimentally derived structure predict electronic band narrowing and a gap at the K point relative to a relaxed model. Multislice pAET simulations further support extending the method to diamond containing a nitrogen-vacancy centre and to amorphous carbon. These results establish pAET for 3D imaging of individual carbon atoms and open a route to linking 3D atomic structure with the properties of light-element materials.

title: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    When anthropogenic CO
                    2
                    emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. The resulting global temperature change, the zero emissions commitment, is central to carbon budget assessments and understanding reversibility of global warming, yet its dependence on prior warming levels remains unclear. Here we show, using zero-emission simulations with the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.2) across global warming levels of 1.5–5 K, that the zero emissions commitment stays near zero up to 2 K but becomes positive at higher warming levels, reaching 0.4–0.6 K after ~ 150 years. This dependence indicates that stabilizing or reversing warming becomes progressively more difficult as peak temperature rises. We identify the mechanism behind this behaviour: stronger warming from higher radiative disequilibrium and weakening carbon sinks, driven by saturated land carbon uptake and the reduced radiative impact of CO
                    2
                    drawdown at higher background CO
                    2
                    concentrations. Higher peak warming therefore commits the planet to additional warming, limiting temperature-overshoot reversibility.

title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting
abstract: The dynamics of isolated quantum systems following a sudden quench has a central role in many areas of material science, high-energy physics and quantum chemistry1-4. Such far-from-equilibrium quantum dynamics-which features complex phenomena with implications for thermalization, non-equilibrium phase transitions and Floquet phase engineering5-8-is challenging to study numerically, in particular, in high-dimensional systems9,10. Here we use a programmable neutral-atom quantum simulator11 to systematically explore quench dynamics in spin models with up to 180 qubits. By initializing the system in a product state and performing quenches across a broad parameter space, we discover several stable, qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes. We trace their robustness to Floquet-like prethermal steady states8 that are stabilized over exponentially long emergent timescales by strong dynamical constraints. We further observe sharp peaks in the dynamical response that are quantitatively explained by the structured melting of prethermalization through resonances. In two dimensions, we uncover a prethermally driven, first-order dynamical phase transition linked to the proliferation of Néel-order defects6,12, and probe it quantitatively using a generalized Clausius-Clapeyron test. Together, these results establish a programmable route to high-energy prethermal phase structure: long-lived dynamical phases, their resonant breakdown and a first-order dynamical phase transition that is not inherited from the equilibrium phase boundaries.
