title: De Novo Design of Catalytically Active Salen-Binding Proteins
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract De novo design of catalytic metalloproteins has the potential to generate enzymes that combine the efficiency of natural proteins with the reactivity of synthetic organometallic catalysts. Here, we develop a computational strategy to design enzymes with novel tertiary structures that bind metal salen complexes, classic small-molecule catalysts not found in biology. Six proteins were designed and screened for function; five of six express well, bind a Co-salen cofactor, and catalyze a transition metal hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated deallylation reaction, representing the first de novo proteins to catalyze this class of transformation. The spectroscopic properties and crystal structure of the most active sequence were in excellent agreement with the design, and the holoprotein retained its structure and activity over a broad range of pH (2–12), temperatures up to 95 °C, and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures. We suggest that the combinatorial space provided by metal ion identity, ligand substitution, and active site structure can be used to generate artificial metalloenzymes that catalyze many chemical transformations.

title: Cation-Effect-Driven Modulation of Interfacial Solvation Structures Enables Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes. With benzyltriethylammonium serving as a model cationic regulator, we show that it accumulates near the polarized graphite surface and forms a cation layer that alters the local electric field. This cation-mediated interfacial regulation promotes PF6– accumulation at the interface, redirects early solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation toward anion-derived pathways, mitigates solvent decomposition, and accelerates Li+ desolvation and transport. As a result, graphite-based pouch cells deliver ∼88.2% state of charge within 6 min, maintain stable cycling for 2000 cycles with ∼71% capacity retention, and provide ∼218.2 Wh kg–1 with 10 min charging. Beyond LiPF6-based electrolytes, this cation effect also promotes reduction of the anions in other lithium-salt systems. This work bridges electrocatalytic cation effects and battery interfacial chemistry, offering a practical route to fast-charging lithium-ion batteries.

title: Localized 4f Magnetism and Low-Lying 5d-Mediated Photoresponses in Layered TmI2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Divalent rare-earth solids with a 4fn+1 configuration provide access to electronic structures in which localized 4f states coexist with low-lying, structurally responsive 5d states, yet the combined magnetic, electrical, and optical manifestations of these states remain underexplored in extended Tm2+ compounds. Here, we investigate layered TmI2 as an extended Tm2+ solid and employ Cs4TmI6 with isolated TmI6 units and dilute SrI2:Tm2+ as targeted reference systems. Structural, spectroscopic, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopic measurements support Tm2+ as the dominant oxidation state, while electronic-structure calculations reveal narrow, localized, occupied Tm 4f-derived bands and low-lying Tm 5d-derived unoccupied states, with substantially greater 5d dispersion in TmI2 than in Cs4TmI6. Magnetic measurements establish localized 4f13 Kramers-ion behavior on the triangular Tm2+ lattice of TmI2, together with a small negative low-temperature Weiss temperature and no evidence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 2 K. Comparative luminescence, photothermal, and photocurrent measurements reveal distinct photoresponses across the three systems within a shared electronic-level framework encompassing 4f–5d and 4f–4f transitions. Relative to Cs4TmI6 and SrI2:Tm2+, TmI2 exhibits a lower-energy optical absorption onset, weaker photoluminescence, and a more pronounced light-induced current response despite its high electrical resistivity. Its wavelength-dependent photothermal response broadly follows the 4f–5d absorption profile. Together, these results establish layered TmI2 as a distinctive rare-earth platform that combines the 4f13 magnetic characteristics familiar from Yb3+ systems with low-energy 4f–5d excitations, expanding the scope for investigating rare-earth magnetic solids with optical excitation channels beyond 4f–4f transitions.

title: Propofol induces sustained suppression of alcohol drinking via habenular activation in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Targeting the lateral habenula (LHb), a key brain region regulating alcohol consumption, presents a promising framework for reducing drinking. LHb neurons exhibit high sensitivity and responsiveness to the intravenous anesthetic propofol. However, whether and how propofol-activated habenular neurons regulate alcohol drinking remains unknown. Here, we show that a single dose of propofol rapidly and persistently reduces alcohol consumption in mice for approximately six days. This effect is mediated by sustained hyperactivity of the habenular ensemble activated by propofol. Furthermore, this ensemble is enriched in 5-HT2C receptors, and we identify the V209 site as the specific binding site through which propofol induces ensemble activation. Disrupting this binding abolishes both the propofol-induced activation of the habenular ensemble and the subsequent reduction in alcohol drinking. Our findings pinpoint a locus of 5-HT2C receptor action within the LHb through which propofol suppresses alcohol consumption, offering a mechanistic framework for understanding alcohol drinking behavior.

title: Geometry-Induced Construction of Sub-Stoichiometric 3D Covalent Organic Frameworks for SO2 Capture
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) have emerged as a rapidly growing class of crystalline porous materials, yet reported structures adhere to the reticular chemistry paradigm of fully connected building blocks. Here, we report a geometry-induced construction strategy that enables the synthesis of sub-stoichiometric 3D COFs─JUC-748, JUC-749, and JUC-750─by deliberately combining building blocks with similar geometries but distinct connectivity. Their structures are determined by continuous rotation electron diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction, revealing that connectivity incompatibility enforces partial condensation and leaves unreacted aldehyde groups periodically arrayed along the pore walls. The frameworks exhibit Brunauer–Emmett–Teller surface areas up to 2836 m2 g–1, and the spatially ordered aldehyde modified pores create a highly favorable adsorption environment for SO2. Remarkably, JUC-748 achieves a SO2 uptake of 16.9 mmol g–1 at 298 K and 1 bar, representing one of the highest values reported for porous organic materials to date. This work establishes geometry-induced construction as a powerful and general strategy for creating intrinsically functionalized 3D COFs with ordered reactive sites, high porosity, and excellent adsorption performance

title: Quantifying Hidden Metabolites in 31P NMR Spectra by Physics-Based Spectral Subtraction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract NMR spectroscopy enables reliable quantification of the metabolites present in a biological sample. The number of metabolites that can be assessed from NMR spectra is often limited by the intrinsically high complexity of the spectra, arising from the large number of molecules paired with their complex spectral patterns. 31P NMR based metabolomics embraces a reduced yet broad view of the metabolism and significantly facilitates the interpretation of the spectra due to a lower number of signals and a larger chemical shift dispersion. However, full quantification of metabolites can still be hindered by the presence of crowded regions. Here we exploit the fact that NMR lineshapes can be simulated precisely from quantum mechanical calculations for disentangling these crowded regions. Iterative subtraction of accurately simulated and fitted spectra of metabolites presenting isolated signals from the experimental spectrum yields meaningful residuals, enabling assignment and quantification of completely hidden metabolites. This approach ended at a noise-level residual spectrum, granting the full quantification of the 31P NMR spectrum. We implemented this approach in MR-SHIFT, a program developed in this work for spin Hamiltonian simulations and spectral fitting, which was then applied to the fully automated analysis of 31P NMR spectra of mouse tissues.

title: Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes. We first overview types of positive feedback relevant to the early evolution of metabolism, the theory of electric field catalysis, and its dominant role in enzyme catalysis. We then examine recent experiments and calculations highlighting the ability of external electric fields to enable nonenzymatic analogues of challenging metabolic reactions in micro- to millisecond reaction times. An underexplored mode of small molecule catalysis (reorientation catalysis) that can only operate in external electric fields is proposed to make positive feedback within prebiotic reaction networks more achievable. By embodying electrostatic catalysis, compartmentalization, and ion concentration gradients, charged aqueous interfaces prepattern three fundamental features of biology, making them a preferred environment for a metabolic origin of life. Making robust progress on the origin of life may surprisingly require exploring the nascent area of electric field-mediated chemistry at aqueous interfaces. Life does not use electric fields to catalyze its metabolic network by accident.

title: Direct Synthesis and Electrochemical Deintercalation of Mg-Intercalated Graphullerite
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) carbon allotropes have unique properties, synthetic tunability, and potential applications across several fields including catalysis, energy storage, and electronics. One such allotrope is the recently discovered graphullerite, which results from the oxidation and deintercalation of the layered rhombohedral fullerene polymer (Mg4C60)∞. The current synthetic approach to (Mg4C60)∞ is limited by low yield, phase impurity, and small crystal size, all of which preclude a comprehensive investigation of the physical and electronic properties of bulk graphullerite and its 2D derivative, graphullerene. Here, we demonstrate two chemical vapor transport methods that produce rhombohedral (Mg4C60)∞ and tetragonal (Mg2C60)∞ as millimeter-sized single crystals with near-complete conversion. Our methods spatially separate the starting materials to circumvent both the thermal decomposition of (Mg4C60)∞ and the significant disparity in vapor pressure between C60 and Mg. We find that using Mg foil results in a near-complete conversion of C60 into a mixture of (Mg4C60)∞ and (Mg2C60)∞. Replacing the foil with Mg2Si produces phase-pure (Mg4C60)∞ with an isolated crystalline yield of 55 to 62%. This high-yielding, phase-pure synthesis enables us to investigate the electrochemical intercalation and deintercalation of Mg2+ into the lattice.

title: Native Mass Spectrometry of Membrane Protein Lipid and Ligand Complexes Using de novo Designed WRAP Domains
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Membrane proteins engage in dynamic transient interactions with surrounding lipids along with their substrates. Capturing these concomitant contacts often remains a challenging problem. Here, we demonstrate that generative deep learning-designed WRAP domains can preserve weak interactions of membrane proteins in native mass spectrometry. Using WRAP-fused GlpG, AqpM, and OmpA as model systems, we show that lipids can bind in multiple positions inside the WRAP, allowing for their characterization by native mass spectrometry. We show that lipid interactions can be altered by changing the WRAP structure. We use the approach to show that WRAP–OmpA binds phosphatidylethanolamine lipids within cavities formed at the protein–WRAP interface, while simultaneously accommodating weak chitobiose ligand binding. These findings establish WRAPs as versatile vehicles to probe ligand and lipid interactions of membrane proteins.

title: Ultrastretchable, Tissue-Matched Piezoelectric Gel with Preferentially Oriented Molecular Ferroelectric Crystallization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular ferroelectrics hold great potential for bioelectronics because of their excellent piezoelectric responses and biocompatibility. However, conventional integration into gel matrices suffers from two major drawbacks: solvent evaporation methods often yield brittle films with poor modulus matching with soft tissues, whereas physical blending typically leads to filler agglomeration and random crystal dispersion, making it difficult to achieve preferential crystal orientation and thereby limiting the piezoelectric performance. Here, we report an in situ crystallization strategy assisted by solvent exchange. This approach enables preferentially oriented triglycine sulfate (TGS) crystals to form within a polyacrylamide (PAM) network reinforced by glycidyl methacrylate-grafted bovine serum albumin (B-G). The B-G macromer strengthens the network through covalent integration and reversible hydrogen-bonding interactions. Subsequent treatment with a choline chloride/sorbitol deep eutectic solvent (DES) induced the preferential orientation of TGS within the gel matrix. The resulting gel achieved a fracture strain exceeding 2800%, maintained mechanical integrity over 10000 loading–unloading cycles, and exhibited mechanical compliance within the range of human soft tissues (10–5–10–4 Pa–1). In vitro and in vivo evaluations further demonstrated favorable biocompatibility and its potential for flexible piezoelectric sensing applications. This work provides molecular-level insight into the design of highly conformable piezoelectric gels containing preferentially oriented molecular ferroelectrics for tissue-matched biointerfaces.

title: Asymmetric Total Syntheses of (+)-Asperterpenoids D and E with a Concurrent Synthesis of ent -(−)-Homoverrucosanol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The first asymmetric total syntheses of sesterterpenoids (+)-asperterpenoids D and E, together with a concurrent synthesis of diterpenoid ent-(−)-homoverrucosanol were achieved from (S)-limonene through a chiral-pool strategy featuring a common late-stage intermediate. Key transformations include a Michael addition and a highly diastereoselective Type I [5 + 2] cycloaddition, which successively establish the C-14 and C-11 methyl-bearing stereocenters with complete stereocontrol. Subsequent oxa-bridge cleavage, cyclopropanation, and A-ring formation via hydroformylation and Carreira cyclopentenal synthesis proceed stereospecifically.

title: The Structure of Oleate-Capped CdSe Nanocrystals Determined by DNP-Enhanced Dipolar Dephasing Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are of interest due to their tunable electronic and optical properties. However, the atomic-level characterization of surface structures of NCs remains an unresolved challenge. Here, we demonstrate that rotational-echo double-resonance (REDOR) experiments can be used to determine structural models of surfaces of CdSe NCs. An atom-efficient ligand-exchange scheme is demonstrated to introduce partially 13C-enriched oleate ligands onto CdSe NCs and enable 13C-dephased REDOR experiments. DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd}, and 111Cd{13C} REDOR NMR experiments were performed on the 13C-enriched oleate-capped zinc blende CdSe NCs. Despite the modest isotope abundance of 77Se and 111Cd, DNP-enhanced 13C{77Se} and 13C{111Cd} REDOR NMR experiments show significant dephasing due to dipolar coupling between 13C atoms and multiple 77Se or 111Cd atoms that are present in the underlying NC lattice. Multispin simulations of 13C{77Se}, 77Se{13C}, 13C{111Cd}, and 111Cd{13C} REDOR curves are performed for different surface structure models, accounting for the structure of the underlying CdSe NC lattice. Based upon these simulations, we propose a structural model of oleate-capped CdSe NCs where chelating carboxylate ligands bind to Cd atoms on {100} zinc blende CdSe surfaces. The combination of REDOR NMR experiments and multispin simulations is a powerful and general method for determining the atomic-level structures of semiconductor NCs and other inorganic materials.

title: Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
abstract: Energy infrastructure requires routine inspection and maintenance to support efficient energy generation, storage, transmission, and distribution. Traditional approaches are often labor-intensive, costly, and hazardous. Advances in robotics and artificial intelligence (AI) enable automated solutions to these challenges. This study systematically reviews robotic technologies for inspecting and maintaining energy infrastructure, including power plants, wind farms, solar farms, refineries, natural gas processing plants, energy storage facilities, oil and gas pipelines, transmission lines, and transformers. A total of 102 journal articles are analyzed and categorized by robotic platforms, sensing modalities, technical approaches, addressed tasks, targeted infrastructure, and evaluation metrics. A keyword-based analysis identifies prevailing research themes and trends. The review highlights several key lessons, such as the strong emphasis on inspection over maintenance and the limited real-world validations. Future directions are discussed from two perspectives: advancing robotic technologies for energy infrastructure and enhancing energy infrastructure management through robotics. This review provides researchers and industry professionals with a structured reference on robotics for improving energy infrastructure resilience and efficiency, supporting future research and deployment.

title: Retrospective single cell lineage tracing with highly mutable homopolymers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Retrospective reconstruction of cell lineages from somatic mutations holds substantial promise for understanding development, tissue homeostasis, and disease. Yet, current approaches are often constrained by low marker density, technical noise, and incomplete molecular readouts that limit the resolution and accuracy of inferred lineages. Here, we present RETrace2, a single-cell dual-omic method for simultaneous lineage tracing and cell-type identification. By identifying and targeting highly mutable homopolymers, which we show are approximately twice as informative as conventional microsatellite repeats, combined with technical improvements to increase marker coverage and reduce experimental errors of reading and amplifying homopolymers, RETrace2 can trace lineage continuously at an estimated resolution of fewer than five cell divisions in microsatellite-unstable organisms. Simultaneously, sparse methylation profiles are obtained from the same cells for cell-type identification. We validate the method using in vitro ground-truth models and demonstrate its utility in vivo by reconstructing multi-organ lineage trees from the brain, kidney and liver of Msh2-deficient mice.

title: Transposable element polymorphisms underlie epigenetic variation and phenotypic diversification during foxtail millet domestication
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs) generate genomic variation, yet how TE polymorphisms reshape the epigenetic landscape and contribute to phenotypic diversification during domestication remains unclear. Here, we show that TE-associated genetic variants drive heritable epigenetic changes underlying key domestication traits in foxtail millet (Setaria italica), one of the oldest cereal crops domesticated in China. By analyzing DNA methylomes from 60 wild and domesticated accessions, we identify 76,815 differentially methylated regions associated with extensive polymorphic TE insertions. Epigenomic variation enables the identification of a TE inventory associated with seed shattering, branching, and growth habits. Functional analyses reveal that two DNA/PIF-Harbinger element insertions in the 5′ UTR of the pleiotropic gene SiGW3 modulate its expression and affect plant architecture, panicle morphology, and grain size. Our findings demonstrate that naturally occurring TE polymorphisms generate heritable epigenetic variation and contribute to phenotypic evolution during crop domestication, with implications for crop improvement.

title: Genome-wide CRISPR screening in Spodoptera frugiperda reveals the determinants of insecticide activation and sensitivity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Insecticide resistance poses a growing threat to global human health and food security. Addressing this challenge requires a comprehensive understanding of the molecular determinants that govern insecticide action and insect sensitivity. However, identifying and functionally validating the specific genes - among the tens of thousands present in a typical insect genome - that contribute to insecticide mode of action and resistance remains a major challenge. Here, we present a genome-wide CRISPR knockout screening system in a cell line derived from Spodoptera frugiperda, a highly damaging insect pest, and demonstrate its utility for dissecting the molecular basis of insecticide activity and resistance. We construct a library of 90,759 single guide RNAs (sgRNAs) targeting 14,434 genes and conduct a three-round screen under successively increasing concentrations of the insecticide pyridalyl. This enriches for the cytochrome P450 gene CYP333B4. Subsequent P450 inhibitor assays, gene knockout in S. frugiperda, and ectopic expression in Drosophila melanogaster confirm that members of the CYP333B subfamily are key mediators of pyridalyl activation and serve as potential resistance targets. Collectively, our findings establish a versatile and scalable platform for genome-wide interrogation of insecticide mode of action and resistance, while uncovering the long-elusive determinants of pyridalyl activity and sensitivity in insects.

title: WASH orchestrates phagosomal maturation and bacterial killing in neutrophils through syntaxin 19-mediated lysosomal fusion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neutrophil phagocytosis is crucial for combating infections, yet the actin-mediated regulation of vesicular trafficking during late phagosomal maturation remains obscure. Using neutrophils lacking the actin nucleation regulator Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome Protein and Scar Homolog (WASH), we identify a mechanism linking actin remodeling, lysosomal fusion, and bacterial killing. Although WASH is dispensable for particle internalization, WASH deficiency impairs lysosome-phagosome fusion and intracellular bacterial killing. Lysosomes from WASH-deficient neutrophils show decreased association with actin comets and impaired dynamics. Rac1 activation rescues lysosomal trafficking but not phagosomal maturation. Mass spectrometry of phagolysosomes and TR-FRET identify atypical syntaxin 19 (STX19) as a WASH binding partner, and WASH recruits STX19 to phagosomes. Reconstituting WASH in primary neutrophils rescues phagocytosis, STX19 interference impairs phagosomal maturation, while STX19 overexpression enhances it. WASH is thus a central mediator of phagosomal maturation through STX19-mediated membrane fusion and actin-driven lysosomal dynamics, revealing how dysregulated trafficking contributes to immunodeficiency.

title: Phosphorylation-driven targeted protein degradation of oncogenic β-catenin
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Therapeutic strategies to inhibit the Wnt signaling pathway for cancer treatment have, so far, failed to advance to the clinic. Induced-proximity drugs are revolutionizing our ability to tackle targets previously considered undruggable. Here, we use an unbiased genome-scale approach to identify induced-proximity protein candidates that inhibit the central Wnt signaling effector β-catenin in colorectal cancer cells. While the identification of several E3 ubiquitin ligases validates our approach, we uncover that inducing proximity to members of the Casein kinase I (CSNK1) family leads to β-catenin degradation and inhibits the growth of colorectal cancer cells harboring Wnt pathway mutations. We show that β-catenin degradation induced by CSNK1 proximity is kinase activity- and proteasome-dependent. We propose that the formation of a neo-degron, through kinase recruitment, can expand induced-proximity drug targeting strategies.

title: Antagonistic second-messenger signalling coordinates Pseudomonas aeruginosa surface colonization and virulence
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Efficient colonisation of host tissue surfaces is a prerequisite for bacterial infection. In the human pathogen Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the second messengers cAMP and c-di-GMP regulate surface behaviours and virulence, but how these pathways are coordinated during tissue infection has remained unclear. Here we demonstrate that cAMP and c-di-GMP establish mutually exclusive signalling states at the single-cell level, generating distinct subpopulations of motile and surface-attached cells through pathway-specific control of type IV pili (T4P). Initial surface contact triggers an increase in c-di-GMP, activating FimW and driving stable attachment via bipolar T4P formation. This state is progressively replaced by cAMP, which inactivates FimW-dependent attachment and induces FimX-mediated T4P polarisation, surface motility and virulence activation. The resulting signalling transition enforces coexisting subpopulations, with attached cells gradually displaced by spreading cells. Using a human airway tissue model, we show that both T4P-mediated adhesion and twitching motility are required for invasion and tissue damage. Based on this, we propose that reciprocal cAMP–c-di-GMP signalling coordinates complementary T4P functions to optimise P. aeruginosa surface colonisation and infection.

title: Structural Evolution of State-Dependent Kinetics during Potassium Storage in Layered CrSe2
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Layered CrSe2 reversibly accommodates approximately one potassium (K) per formula unit, but the structural origin of its rate-dependent capacity remains unresolved. Operando synchrotron X-ray diffraction (SXRD) reveals the sequential P-3m1-R3m-C2/m phase pathway during cycling at different current rates. The P-3m1/R3m transformation exhibits the lattice discontinuity and becomes incomplete when increasing the current rate, as directly observed by operando SXRD. Chemical K deintercalation and state-resolved impedance measurements provide complementary evidence for sluggish kinetics near the fully deintercalated regime. Restricting the upper cutoff voltage will sacrifice some capacity but will improve electrochemical cycling capacity retention. These findings identify a particularly rate-sensitive structural region and show how phase-resolved characterization can guide voltage-window selection for layered potassium-storage electrodes.

title: Soft robotic and computational models of left atrial hemodynamics in sinus rhythm and atrial fibrillation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Atrial fibrillation poses significant challenges because the complex geometry of the left atrial appendage complicates personalized interventions for stroke prevention. Current reliance on animals and cadavers raises reproducibility concerns, necessitating the development of high fidelity, physiologically relevant tools. To address this, we develop a multimodal framework including a soft robotic benchtop simulator and a lumped parameter computational model to replicate left atrial function. The system integrates patient-specific geometries with soft robotic actuators to reproduce realistic wall motion and hemodynamics. Complementary lumped parameter model provides mechanistic insights, quantifying systemic hemodynamic changes during disease and interventions. The models effectively replicate the clinical markers of atrial dysfunction and arrhythmia disorders, and their accuracy is demonstrated through validation against human imaging and porcine models. We show that this scalable, versatile experimental and computational framework advances cardiovascular biomechanics, enabling device development, clinical research and training, and personalized atrial fibrillation treatment to improve patient outcomes.

title: Ultra-high precision speckle spectrometer enabling radio-frequency scale resolution of atomic spectra
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Laser speckle, the granular intensity pattern arising from random optical interference, provides a high-dimensional encoding of spectral information that can be exploited for precision metrology. Speckle-based spectrometers have advanced rapidly owing to their compact footprint, mechanical robustness and alignment agnostic nature, yet their spectral resolution has remained limited to the picometre scale. In this work, we break this limit by employing an integrating sphere as a multiply scattering cavity with access to a high range of path lengths to enhance spectral sensitivity. At 780 nm, the resulting device achieves a resolution of 6 fm, corresponding to a resolving power of 1.3 × 108, representing an approximately 80-fold improvement over previous implementations. This ultra-high resolution enables clear discrimination of laser sidebands generated by an electro-optical modulator, with extracted sideband powers agreeing with expected values to within 1%. It further permits a direct speckle-based measurement of the hyperfine structure of the D2 transition in 85Rb, with transmission spectra differing by no more than 3.7% from independent wavemeter-referenced measurements. These results establish speckle as a platform for ultra-high precision spectroscopy, radio-frequency spectrometry, and microwave photonics.

title: Coupling electrolyte mechanical reinforcement and interfacial stress relaxation for near-ambient sulfide all-solid-state lithium metal batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: All-solid-state lithium metal batteries offer the promise of higher energy density and improved safety compared with conventional lithium-ion batteries; however, their practical operation at room temperature and low stack pressures ( ~ 0.1 MPa) remains challenging due to lithium dendrite formation and stress-induced interfacial degradation. Herein, we demonstrate near-ambient operation ( ≤ 0.3 MPa, room temperature) of all-solid-state lithium metal batteries through a combined electrolyte–current collector design. A self-polymerizable thioctic acid-modified composite solid electrolyte suppresses internal lithium metal creep with high stress tolerance, while a porous carbon matrix current collector provides localized stress relaxation and accommodates lithium deposition within internal voids. As a result, stable long-term cycling is achieved under near-ambient conditions even at a high areal loading of 2.4 mAh cm−2 using a LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 positive electrode operated at 0.1 C. These findings highlight the importance of controlling lithium deformation and stress relaxation for the development of practical all-solid-state lithium metal batteries.

title: Topological Josephson trijunctions as a Majorana source and path
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Majorana bound states (MBSs) are zero-energy localized states in topological superconductors, obeying non-Abelian braiding statistics. Manipulation of mobile MBSs, encompassing their on-demand generation, propagation, and fusion, is essential for braiding MBSs and operating topological qubits. We show that the manipulation is enabled by a trijunction formed on a topological insulator in a perpendicular magnetic field, where three Josephson junctions meet. While the superconducting phases at the trijunction center evolve to cross a boundary between topological and non-topological phase domains, the trijunction offers two distinct dynamics, source/sink and path, depending on the phase boundaries. At a source/sink boundary, two MBSs are pairwise generated at the center, and one of them is ejected to a Josephson junction. The reverse, pair annihilation by collision of two MBSs, can also happen. At a path boundary, an MBS moves from a Josephson junction to the trijunction center or vice versa, without involving other MBSs. Exploiting the two dynamics, fusion and braiding of MBSs can be operated in a trijunction network. We illustrate this with a double trijunction setup, where non-Abelian state evolutions associated with MBSs can be manipulated without dynamical control of the setup and detected by Josephson emission spectroscopy.

title: CO2 responsive nanoscopic and macroscopic materials directed by peptides
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Stimuli such as pH, light, and electromagnetic fields have enabled precise control over nanoscale interactions, yet gases remain relatively unexplored as regulators of material behavior despite their central roles in biology, energy, and climate. Here, we introduce carbon dioxide (CO2) as a dynamic and reversible stimulus for controlling nanoscale and macroscale matter using sequence-specific peptide design. Peptide-functionalized nanoparticles exhibit pronounced and tunable responses to CO2 across orders of magnitude changes in gas flow rate, with sensitivity governed by site- and sequence-specific changes in peptide structure. The aggregation sequence-dependence is described by six design principles while quantitative modeling show that aggregation rate scales with flow rate rather than cumulative CO2 dose. This gas-controlled response translates from colloidal nanoparticles to cm-scale biocompatible hydrogels that reversibly and colorimetrically respond to CO2. Leveraging this responsiveness, we further demonstrate spatial patterning of a hydrogel through a gas-permeable mask using CO2 as a lithographic stimulus. Consequently, this work establishes gas-mediated control as a general and scalable strategy for programming responsive materials across length scales.

title: Selective depolymerization of poly(ethylene terephthalate) for economical closed-loop recycling of mixed textiles
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is the second largest source of plastic wastes. An ideal solution is to chemically convert PET back into its monomers. Although many strategies have been reported, their extension towards PET-containing waste textiles is economically prohibitive. This is because chemical depolymerization can degrade multiple components in mixed textiles, yielding complex mixtures that are cost-prohibitive to separate and purify. Here, we report highly efficient processes that overcome this bottleneck. We find that, for thermally treated mixed textiles, the depolymerization of PET via methanolysis can be achieved in a rapid yet highly selective manner under mild conditions. This greatly simplifies the chemical recycling process, yielding high-purity DMT monomer ( ≥ 99.92%) at a yield of 91%. Techno-economic analysis shows that our strategy is economically competitive, suggesting a feasible closed-loop option for this indispensable commodity polymer.

title: Nanofluid wetting of Cu enables thin lithium negative electrodes for high-energy and long-cycling lithium metal batteries
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Exploiting thin Li foils ≤ 20 μm is required for high-energy-density and long-cycling-lifespan battery, but is severely hindered by the poor processability of Li, as well as its inhomogeneous plating behaviors and resulting low Coulombic efficiency. Herein, an approach balancing Li supply and consumption is fulfilled by designing thin molten-salt-derived, nanocomposite Li@LiX metal negative electrodes. Benefitting from the formation of nanofluid due to the spontaneous reaction of inorganic nanoparticles in molten Li, the bonding states at both Li surface and Li|Cu interface are effectively regulated, displaying an enhanced wetting behaviour of Li on Cu. This approach enables the fabrication of an 800-nm-thick Li-based negative electrode foil as well as the formation of an inorganic-rich interphase upon cycling, which suppresses Li consumption by reducing corrosion susceptibility. As a result, practical pouch cells composed of 10-μm-thick Li@lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) and LiFePO4 offer stable cycling over 250 cycles, while those composed of 20-μm-thick Li@LiFSI and LiNi0.92Co0.03Mn0.05O2 with an areal capacity of 4.6 mAh cm−2 achieve 100 cycles, yielding specific energy of 498 Wh kg−1 and energy density of 1,142 Wh L−1, indicating that this design strategy is applicable to lithium metal batteries.

title: Fully Integrated Deep-Ocean Flexible Temperature–Depth Sensor with Neural Network Compensation
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Earth’s deep ocean shapes global heat transport, carbon cycling and abyssal circulation, yet large regions remain undersampled. While conventional instruments provide precise single point measurements, their rigidity and weight limit deployment on emerging platforms that could extend observational reach. Here, we introduce the fully integrated, flexible temperature–depth sensor deployable on curved and mobile surfaces for deep-sea measurements. The compact, lightweight, stress-adaptive low-power electronics (average quiescent current: 24.63 µA) unit operates as a co-designed cyber–physical platform, where the porous laser-induced graphene–polydimethylsiloxane composite sensing element achieves a broad measurement range over 0–10 MPa hydrostatic pressure, while temperature–pressure compensation through a dual-hidden-layer neural network combined with polynomial fitting yields a depth error of ≤±0.91% full scale and temperature accuracy of ≤±0.29 °C. Deep-sea trials to 4812.2 m show structural integrity under ~50 MPa hydrostatic pressure, demonstrating durability in extreme environments and enabling sensing on platforms inaccessible to conventional instruments.

title: Fractional quantum Hall states and oscillatory Landau charge squeezing in Bernal tetralayer graphene
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The precise layer-number control in graphene provides valuable opportunities to explore the physics from the two-dimensional limit to the bulk crystalline regime. As the thickness increases, a fundamental question is how this increased dimensionality influences the integer and fractional quantum Hall states. Here, we perform magnetotransport measurements on high-quality Bernal tetralayer graphene and uncover a variety of fractional quantum Hall states at filling factors with both odd-denominator and even ones (ν − 1/2 = 3, 5, 7, 8, 10), which may be non-Abelian states. Moreover, the fractional quantum Hall states exhibit a sawtooth pattern when an out-of-plane displacement field D is tuned. Theoretical calculations reveal that these patterns arise from oscillatory Landau charge squeezing effect caused by subtle competitions between Landau levels with vastly disparate spatial distributions. Our results establish Bernal tetralayer graphene as a promising platform, where the layer degree of freedom provides distinctive tunability to explore rich correlated phenomena.

title: Mapping Future Energy Journeys Through Modeling the Global Transport of Synthetic Energy Carriers
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Synthetic energy carriers can connect renewable-energy-rich potential production regions with distant demand centers, but the emergence of trade depends on total supply costs. Here, we develop a spatially resolved heuristic combining hydrogen production costs with ports, pipelines, and shipping routes, as well as syntheses, cracking, and reformation processes, to identify key import corridors. Across 10,883 production locations and seven different scenarios, we find that export regions connected to the importer through retrofit-ready pipelines remain competitive despite only moderate renewable potentials. Meanwhile, for remote exporters competitiveness depends on port availability and coastal access through pipeline networks. Gaseous hydrogen dominates short pipeline routes, and ammonia is preferred for maritime trade, whereas methanol and methane emerge in long multimodal chains. Additional results show that low-cost heat availability is required for the competitiveness of liquid organic hydrogen carriers, while accounting for market values of conventional counterparts boosts ammonia and methanol trade.

title: Insular motor and error encoding supports self-correcting intracranial brain-computer interface
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Error recognition is fundamental to adaptive behavior, enabling rapid compensatory action when outcomes deviate from expectations. Central to this function are neural circuits for performance monitoring, encoding cognitive signals that could support more reliable neural interfaces. Here, we recorded intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) in epilepsy patients to enable a motor brain-computer interface (BCI) while sampling error-related activity across a distributed network. Our work reveals high-frequency population dynamics emerging in the anterior insula and propagating to the prefrontal cortex as the interface fails to follow the user’s intention. We identify spatially organized insular responses to error processing and movement feedback, highlighting it as a heterogeneous hub linking action and outcome. Frontoinsular recording sites were found to preferentially encode error-related activity, while centroparietal responses were intermixed with compensatory motor signals, making the former a compelling target for real-time error correction. Together, our findings demonstrate a human intracranial BCI harnessing insular brain activity, integrating cognitive processes directly into device control.

title: Cu─Cu Dimerization Suppresses Pseudo‐Jahn–Teller Distortion to Enhance Electroluminescence in Tricoordinate Clusters
abstract: ABSTRACT Copper(I) emitters are promising low‐cost and high‐efficiency electroluminescent (EL) materials for large‐scale applications, but their performances are limited by severe nonradiative quenching due to excited‐state structural relaxation. Tricoordinate Cu(I) systems with trigonal geometries are believed to be superior in excited‐state structural stability, but still suffer from pseudo‐Jahn–Teller distortion. Here we report tricoordinate Cu 2 clusters with Cu─Cu dimerization to alleviate the pseudo‐Jahn–Teller effect and enhance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF). Through further introduction of electron‐donating and rigid phenoxazine (PXZ) groups, [DPXZCzDP] 2 Cu 2 exhibits ligand‐centered excited states and multiple reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) channels, giving rise to the outstanding photoluminescence quantum yield of 91% and a record external quantum efficiency of ∼24.6% among tricoordinate Cu(I) emitters, accompanied by reduced efficiency roll‐off. This work validates combined ligand and coordination engineering as a robust strategy to boost luminescence performance of Cu(I) systems and advances low‐cost, high‐efficiency cluster light‐emitting devices for practical display and lighting applications.

title: A Dicationic Diradicaloid through Intramolecular One‐Electron Transfer from a B‐B σ‐Bond to an Aromatic π‐System
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein we report on a novel type of main group diradicaloid with the triplet state arising from unprecedented reversible intramolecular one‐electron transfer from a B‐B σ‐bond (HOMO) into a boron‐bound organic π‐acceptor orbital (LUMO of pyrazine). The deep‐red bis(diboranyl)pyrazine dication, with a bridging pyrazine between two diboranyl units and sp 3 ‐hybridised boron atoms, represents also the first example for a fully‐reversible thermal redox equilibrium between a diborane as electron donor and an organic π‐acceptor. The compound is stable in solution and in the solid state under ambient conditions. Two modified systems were synthesised, demonstrating that a decrease of the B‐B σ‐bond orbital energy as well as an increase of the π*‐acceptor orbital energy leads to an extinction of the diradicaloid character.

title: Conjugation‐Activity Regulated Molecular Templates Enable Microcrystallite‐Refined Hard Carbon for High‐Performance Sodium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT The microcrystallite structure of carbon materials has a significant impact on their electrochemical properties, yet it usually suffers from uncontrollable aromatic ordering and thickening during carbonization. Here, we develop a conjugation‐activity regulated molecular template strategy to program the microcrystallite evolution of coal‐derived hard carbon toward sodium storage. By modulating conjugation capacity and bond–cleavage thresholds of aromatic N‐heterocycles, we propose a molecular template design principle: strong conjugation creates supplementary microcrystallite growth sites to alter aromatic domain evolution, while molecular activity controls the effective activation range for conjugation‐mediated reconstruction. N‐Phenylcarbazole, which integrates a sufficiently conjugated aromatic core with a locally labile N‐phenyl linkage, realizes this balance by enabling radical‐mediated precursor reconstruction during pre‐oxidation and constrained aromatic‐layer rearrangement during carbonization. The resulting hard carbon exhibits refined and dispersed turbostratic microcrystallites with enlarged interlayer spacing and regulated defects, retaining 250.3 mAh g −1 after 5600 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , corresponding to 83.6% capacity retention. This work establishes an activity‐window‐modulated conjugated‐molecule design principle for programming coal‐derived carbon microcrystallites.

title: A General Deep Eutectic Solvent‐Mediated Scalable Preparation of Halide Solid‐State Electrolytes for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT In the pursuit of high‐energy‐density all‐solid‐state lithium batteries, halide solid‐state electrolytes (HSSEs) have attracted increasing interest due to their high ionic conductivity and superior high‐voltage stability. Developing cost‐effective and scalable preparation methods is essential for their practical deployment, yet the current mainstream solid‐state preparation routes either require stringent environmental control with prohibitive costs or suffer from low efficiency. Herein, we report a universal deep eutectic solvent (DES)‐mediated wet‐chemical method that enables the efficient and scalable preparation of HSSEs. Taking Li 3 YCl 6 as a typical HSSE, we revealed the competitive coordination and hydrogen‐bond formation mechanisms through combined modeling and experiments. This method shows low cost, and good scalability for various HSSEs, and the resultant HSSEs show a similar conductivity (>0.30 mS cm −1 ) as that prepared by the solid‐state mechanical method. Notably, the humidity‐degraded HSSEs can also be readily regenerated by this method. The all‐solid‐state lithium batteries assembled with the resultant Li 3 YCl 6 deliver impressive performance, achieving a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 98.6% with a LiCoO 2 cathode and a remarkable discharge capacity of 195.9 mAh g −1 with a single‐crystal LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 cathode. This work establishes a new paradigm for the sustainable and scalable manufacturing of HSSEs for next‐generation all‐solid‐state batteries.
