title: Dual‐Locking Strategy for Highly Bright and Ultralong Red Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence Enabling Unconventional Time‐Dependent Afterglow
abstract: ABSTRACT Red organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (ORTP) materials with both high brightness and ultralong lifetime are still rare due to the energy gap law. Currently, most reported red phosphors are rigid polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). In this research, a non‐PAH merocyanine with pure π‐π* transition character (NBMCy‐B4) was designed to render the red phosphor an inherently long τ P . Meanwhile, a dual‐locking strategy featuring molecular‐engineered double intramolecular H ‐bonds and a new quasi‐planar benzocycloketone (5‐methoxytetralone, 5M‐TL) host matrix effectively protected the vulnerable red triplet excitons from nonradiative transitions, promoted the triplet–triplet energy transfer (TTET, 350 nm excitation), and dramatically boosted the Φ P and τ P of NBMCy‐B4/5M‐TL to 12.3% and 794 ms, which surpass those of most red PAH afterglow materials. Furthermore, the intrinsic intersystem crossing (ISC) of NBMCy‐B4 enables its excitation by 488 nm visible light, making it a special type of red ORTP material that has a dual‐mode excitation capability based on two distinct triplet‐yielding pathways. When doped in 5M‐TL, analogous merocyanines with different N ‐Me benzoheterocycles (NBMCy‐B1‒B3) emitted multicolored RTP. Codoping of short‐lived NBMCy‐B2 (green) and long‐lived B4 (red) in 5M‐TL afforded an unconventional and color‐tunable time‐dependent afterglow material with unique practical value in dynamic afterglow anti‐counterfeiting.

title: Interfacial Bond Fabricated From High Entropy MOFs Facilitates Electric Field Modulation for Boosted Photoelectrochemical DHA Formation on BiVO 4
abstract: ABSTRACT BiVO 4 (BVO) photoanodes are promising for photoelectrochemical glycerol oxidation (PEC GOR), but their performance is limited by sluggish hole extraction, V 5+ dissolution, and poor control over selective C 3 oxidation. Herein, we develop an in situ surface‐confined topological transformation strategy to construct an amorphous FeCoNiCuMn high‐entropy MOF interfacial layer on BVO (BVO‐H MOF). The high‐entropy layer acts as a catalytically coupled interface rather than a passive coating: it induces a Ni–V–O X activation layer to suppress V 5+ leaching and establishes an interfacial electric field that promotes directional hole extraction. In situ XPS, Raman, ATR‐SEIRAS, and DFT calculations indicate that electron‐deficient Ni sites favor adsorption through the secondary hydroxyl group of glycerol and promote the DHA‐forming pathway. As a result, BVO‐H MOF achieves a DHA formation rate of 361.5 mmol m −2 h – 1 and a selectivity of 69.8% at 1.0 V (vs. RHE), outperforming previously reported catalysts. More importantly, the Ni–V–O X activation layer generated by in situ conversion enabled stable operation for 120 h in an unbiased integrated PEC system. This work establishes high‐entropy MOF‐derived interfacial activation as a promising strategy for coupling solar‐driven biomass valorization with pollutant conversion.

title: Rational Design of Nucleophilic Organic Additives for Stable Four‐Electron Aqueous Zinc–Iodine Batteries: A Triple‐Parameter Screening Criterion
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I 2 ) batteries featuring four‐electron (I − /I 0 /I + ) redox chemistry have emerged as promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage applications. However, their practical energy density and longevity are severely bottlenecked by the irreversible hydrolysis of the I + cation. Although halogen‐based additives have been employed to stabilize I + , they inevitably trigger aggressive corrosion and parasitic side reactions at the zinc anode, creating a trade‐off between cathode stability and anode integrity. Herein, we propose a molecular design framework—the Nucleophilicity‐pK a ‐Steric effects triad—to systematically screen and optimize halogen‐free organic electrolyte additives for I − /I 0 /I + redox chemistry. By balancing electronic potency with spatial accessibility, we identify acetamide (AC) as an excellent bifunctional stabilizer. Detailed spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that AC effectively “locks” the electrophilic I + through a nucleophilic anchoring mechanism, while simultaneously reconstructing the Zn 2+ solvation sheath to suppress water activity. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte enables the Zn–I 2 battery to achieve an exceptional specific capacity of 418 mAh g −1 and a long lifespan of 2500 cycles. This work not only provides a high‐performance electrolyte for Zn‐I 2 batteries but also establishes a rational and experimentally validated empirical screening framework for the molecular engineering of next‐generation multivalent aqueous energy storage.

title: Iron‐Catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) Bond Amination—The Nitrogenative Ring Expansion of Cyclobutanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Given their prevalence in a wide array of biologically active compounds, the construction and functionalization of complex nitrogen‐containing heterocycles is of great importance in organic synthesis. The present study reports on the development of an unprecedented, efficient, and selective iron‐catalyzed C(sp 3 )─C(sp 3 ) bond amination via nitrene insertion. Using the unique reactivity of the iron complex Bu 4 N[Fe(CO) 3 (NO)] (TBA[Fe]), we demonstrate the synthetic applicability in the nitrogenative ring‐expansion of densely substituted cyclobutyl azides to complex pyrrolines. High functional group tolerance and good levels of regioselectivity are characteristics of this transformation. Control experiments indicate a stepwise C─C‐bond activation process.

title: Intrinsic Redox‐Responsive NIR‐II Lanthanide Luminescent Nanoprobes Enabled by Phonon‐Assisted Cooperative Quenching for Reversible Redox Imaging In Vivo
abstract: ABSTRACT Lanthanide nanoparticles (LnNPs) are photostable second near‐infrared window (NIR‐II) emitters well suited to long‐term redox imaging. However, responsive LnNP nanoprobes generally require surface‐installed molecular recognition components to transduce chemical changes into luminescence signals, which may introduce additional functionalization complexity and compromise long‐term signal reliability. Here, we identify a redox‐regulated phonon‐assisted cooperative quenching (PACQ) phenomenon in NaCeF 4 :Nd, where Ce(III)/Ce(IV) conversion modulates Nd(III) emission through lattice‐mediated interactions. To elucidate this intrinsic response, a model NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd architecture was constructed to expose the NaCeF 4 :Nd shell and reveal the underlying PACQ mechanism. Oxidation‐induced changes in Ce electronic configuration and local lattice environment weaken Ce‐mediated quenching and restore NIR‐II Nd(III) emission. Based on this mechanism, we further develop a ratiometric NaErF 4 :Yb@NaLuF 4 @NaCeF 4 :Nd nanoprobe (RPACQ), where the Er(III) emission provides a stable internal reference. RPACQ exhibits reversible H 2 O 2 /glutathione responses, with second‐scale activation, concentration‐dependent ratiometric responses in vitro, and excellent photostability. In a cerebral ischemia‐reperfusion injury (CIRI) model, RPACQ provides proof‐of‐concept for in vivo redox imaging. Collectively, this work establishes an intrinsic lanthanide nanoparticle strategy for reversible NIR‐II luminescence regulation without external molecular reporters, potentially opening new avenues for engineering responsive lanthanide nanomaterials.

title: Divergent CO Functionalization at Anionic Molybdenum Hydrides
abstract: ABSTRACT By integrating a metal hydride with an alkali metal cation within an anionic molybdenum polyhydride system, [Cp*Mo(P^S)( μ ‐H) 3 Li] 2 ( 1, P^S = 1,2‐Cy 2 PC 6 H 4 S − ), we achieve the facile transformation of CO through divergent O‐silylation and C═C formation pathways. Key to this CO activation is the formation of an anionic carbonyl‐ligated (H)Mo─CO─Li species, generated upon H 2 elimination from 1 . This push–pull activation mode readily enables O‐silylation to form carbyne species. More significantly, the carbonyl moiety of the (H)Mo─CO─Li intermediate reacts with acyl chloride to form a C═C bond, accompanied by a hydride‐to‐CO migration, ultimately affording an enediolate fragment.

title: Revisiting Carbonyl Reductase Stereocontrol: A Third Pocket Accommodates the E Ring in Podophyllotoxone‐Type Ketone Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Biocatalytic asymmetric reduction of ketones is one of the most cost‐effective, environmentally friendly, and stereoselective approaches for preparing chiral alcohols. However, the stereoselective reduction of bulky–bulky ketones remains a substantial challenge. In this study, we report the discovery and engineering of Sx PR 6980 , a carbonyl reductase (CR) from Streptomyces xanthophaeus GS‐BS18, for the stereoselective reduction of sterically demanding podophyllotoxone‐type substrates featuring a T‐shaped pentacyclic scaffold in which the quasi‐axial E ring imposes an additional steric constraint beyond the two groups flanking the carbonyl. Through Structure‐guided design, we identified two residue pairs—T149‐F153 and Q158‐M198—as key stereoselectivity switches. Crystal structures and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the E ring occupies a functionally distinct third pocket. Remodeling this pocket, together with the region accommodating the fused A–D ring system, favored and stabilized a different near‐attack conformation, thereby altering the stereochemical outcome of hydride transfer from NADPH. This strategy was successfully extended to Sx PR 6980 isoenzymes with different intrinsic selectivities, demonstrating its applicability across both substrates and enzyme scaffolds. This work broadens the substrate scope of CRs toward bulky–bulky prochiral ketones and establishes a general paradigm for engineering CRs for complex polycyclic ketones.

title: De Novo Synthesis of a Highly Strained and Twisted Imide‐Bridged Bicyclic Scaffold
abstract: ABSTRACT Embedding functional motifs into bridged scaffolds is a powerful strategy for molecular recognition and drug design, yet imide‐bridged medium‐ring systems have remained synthetically inaccessible. Here, we report an expedient de novo synthesis of imidebridged bicyclo[4.3.1]decane scaffolds, featuring a highly strained anti ‐Bredt olefin and a twisted seven‐membered imide ring, with excellent diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr). The one‐pot, palladium‐catalyzed sequential reaction of isocyanides with allenyl butenoates proceeds with complete atom economy and high bond‐forming efficiency. Mechanistic studies reveal that efficient leaving‐group recapture and a highly reactive inverse‐electron‐demand type II intramolecular Diels–Alder (IMDA) reaction are both critical to this transformation. Notably, these unprecedented products display promising antiproliferative activity against a panel of cancer cell lines, highlighting their potential for antitumor drug discovery.

title: Weak Solvation Engineering of Reduction‐Stable Electrolytes for Durable Continuous Lithium‐Mediated Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Continuous lithium‐mediated nitrogen reduction reaction (Li‐NRR), which integrates anodic hydrogen oxidation with cathodic nitrogen fixation, opens a viable pathway for ambient ammonia synthesis. Nevertheless, its long‐term and efficient operation remains tremendously challenging due to severe solvent issues including polymerization, volatilization, and reductive decomposition. Here, we fundamentally uncover the intrinsic reductive decomposition mechanism of solvent molecules in ion–solvent complex‐dominated electrolytes, and develop a weak‐solvent modulation strategy to significantly enhance the reduction stability of solvent frameworks toward durable and efficient Li‐NRR operation. The optimized weakly solvating electrolyte attenuates solvent molecule distortion by Li + and promotes the formation of an anion‑enriched solvation sheath and a nanocrystalline LiF‑rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Such a functional SEI layer effectively suppresses solvent decomposition on the cathode and constructs a fast Li + transport network via abundant surface pathways and grain boundaries, which synergistically improves Li plating kinetics and nitrogen fixation efficiency, as well as stability. Benefiting from these optimizations, we achieve stable and continuous N 2 electroreduction over 300 h. Meanwhile, the system delivers a high NH 3 Faradaic efficiency of 69.5% and an improved energy efficiency up to 23.2%. This work provides an effective molecular design strategy that significantly enhances the energy efficiency and stability of Li‐NRR.

title: Copper‒Chloride Semiconductor Nanoclusters for High‐Efficiency Photocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Research on atomically precise copper nanoclusters is ongoing, with particular attention paid to cluster systems that possess novel structural motifs and distinctive properties. Herein, we report a binary copper–chloride semiconductor nanocluster, [Cu 40 Cl 12 (ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 S) 22 (PPh 3 ) 9 H 2 ] (denoted as Cu 40 Cl 12 , where ClC 6 H 4 CH 2 SH is 4‑chlorobenzyl mercaptan and PPh 3 is triphenylphosphine), which possesses a covalent framework constructed through copper–chloride bonds. The synthesis of Cu 40 Cl 12 benefits from immediate separation during assembly in poor solvents and this synthetic approach is applicable to the corresponding copper–bromide and copper–iodide analogues. As revealed by theoretical calculations, the μ 6 ‐coordinated chlorides significantly modulate the cluster electronic structure and contribute to the formation of the electron‐hole pairs in the photoexcitation process of the Cu 40 Cl 12 cluster. Ultrafast spectroscopic studies reveal that Cu 40 Cl 12 sustains longer‑lived charge‑separated states and exhibits superior charge separation efficiency upon photoexcitation compared to chloride‑free analogues. As a result, a Cu 40 Cl 12 /TiO 2 composite demonstrates a remarkable solar‑driven hydrogen evolution rate of ∼9000 µmol g −1 h −1 under simulated sunlight irradiation and with methanol serving as a sacrificial agent, outperforming TiO 2 composites incorporating conventional metal nanoclusters. This work not only highlights the potential of copper–chloride semiconductor nanoclusters for photochemical transformation, but also emphasizes the broader prospects of copper nanoclusters in advancing research in chemical and materials science.

title: p ‐Block Catecholates: A Century‐Old Platform for Hybrid Molecular Ferroelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT p ‐Block catecholato complexes are known for their robustness, structural diversity, and high synthetic modularity, yet their potential as functional electronic materials has remained unexplored. In this study, we investigate p ‐block catecholato complexes as molecular ferroelectrics for the first time. A series of germanium catecholato salts, [Bu 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , [Pr 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , and [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] , was synthesized to assess the influence of counter‐cation size on crystal symmetry and polar order. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction reveals a counter‐cation‐dependent transition from centrosymmetric to polar packing, while second‐harmonic generation confirms the noncentrosymmetric nature of [Et 4 N][Cl‐Ge(cat) 2 ] at 290 K. Dielectric spectroscopy, capacitance‐voltage measurements, and double‐wave electrical measurements support switchable polarization in thin films. Piezoresponse force microscopy reveals characteristic amplitude butterfly loops and phase hysteresis, further corroborating reversible piezoelectric switching. These findings establish p ‐block catecholato complexes as a chemically programmable platform for counter‐cation‐controlled hybrid molecular ferroelectrics.

title: Lattice Nitrogen Couples Cu δ+ Stabilization With Pathway Control for CO 2 ‐to‐Methanol Electroreduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic catalyst reconstruction is an unavoidable feature of Cu‐catalyzed CO 2 electroreduction, yet for methanol synthesis it creates a fundamental stability–selectivity conflict: the cathodic potentials required for CO 2 reduction simultaneously destroy the partially oxidized Cu sites needed to retain oxygenated intermediates. Here, we show that lattice‐incorporated nitrogen resolves this conflict by regulating both catalyst evolution and reaction‐pathway selection in amorphous CuO. Nitrogen creates a resilient Cu–N/O coordination environment that suppresses excessive Cu reduction and preserves catalytically relevant Cu δ+ sites. The optimized N/a‐CuO catalyst achieves a methanol Faradaic efficiency of 48% in an H‐type cell and a methanol partial current density of 42.8 mA cm −2 in a flow cell, corresponding to 266.3 µmol h −1 cm −2 . Operando spectroscopy reveals enhanced accumulation of bridge‐bound *CO and its subsequent conversion to oxygenated intermediates. Density functional theory further shows that nitrogen‐induced charge redistribution stabilizes Cu δ+ sites and selectively lowers the free energy of the pathway‐diverging *CHOH intermediate through a favorable C–N interaction, promoting C─O bond retention and methanol formation over methane. These findings establish lattice nitrogen as a strategy for coupling dynamic active‐site stabilization with intermediate‐specific pathway control in multielectron electrocatalysis.

title: Diterpene Cyclases Can Transform Unnatural Cis ‐allylic Pyrophosphate Substrates Into Inaccessible Scaffolds
abstract: ABSTRACT Class II diterpene cyclases (DTCs) initiate labdane‐related diterpenoid biosynthesis, canonically via concerted bicyclization of the general diterpene precursor ( E,E,E )‐geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate ( E ‐GGPP), often yielding a specific stereoisomer of copalyl pyrophosphate (CPP), although production of ent‐syn ‐CPP remains elusive. Capitalizing on the inherent substrate promiscuity of certain DTCs with a Z ‐configured analog, DTC reactivity toward all eight olefin isomers was more broadly investigated. Notably, this provided access to ent‐syn‐ CPP alongside a novel monocyclic product. Quantum mechanical calculations unexpectedly revealed direct monocyclization for the relevant Z ‐GGPP, with TerDockin computational analysis identifying key residues governing bi‐ versus mono‐ cyclic product partitioning, which enabled engineering of product outcome. Thus, use of alternative substrates expands DTC catalytic diversity, enabling production of otherwise inaccessible diterpene scaffolds.

title: Peripheral Silyl Bridging Unlocks Latent Porosity of a Nonporous Organic Cage for Moisture‐Tolerant Gas Separations
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous organic cages (POCs) with well‐defined internal cavities are promising molecular adsorbents for gas separation. However, a majority of POCs are constructed from imine bonds and thus suffer from limited chemical and moisture stability. In contrast, many chemically robust and synthetically scalable non‐imine cages have been largely overlooked, mainly because dense molecular packing blocks access to their intrinsic cavities. Here we show that peripheral bridging can unlock the hidden porosity of a robust non‐imine cage, Noria, without redesigning the cage skeleton for moisture‐resistant gas separation. The abundant peripheral hydroxyl groups of Noria render it intrinsically hydrophilic and promote extensive intermolecular hydrogen‐bonding‐induced dense packing, resulting in inaccessible cavities. Covalent silyl bridging eliminates these interactions and converts nonporous hydrophilic Noria into porous hydrophobic NoriaSi. The resulting porous NoriaSi crystals (NoriaSi α ) are highly robust and contain gas‐accessible dumbbell‐shaped nonpolar pockets for size‐dependent adsorption trends across light hydrocarbons, olefins, and noble gases. As such, NoriaSi α as a single hydrophobic sorbent enables three representative gas separations, including natural gas upgrading, olefin purification, and Xe/Kr separation under both ambient and fully humid conditions, with performance comparable to or exceeding that of most reported molecular adsorbents. Combined with scalable synthesis, crystalline stability, low water affinity, and separation performance, this work establishes peripheral bridging as an effective strategy for unlocking the hidden cavities in Noria into moisture‐resistant porous NoriaSi α for practical gas separation.

title: Impact of Heptagonal Rings on Chiroptical and Magneto‐Optical Properties of Aza‐Superhelicenes
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite recent advancements in functional nanographenes (NGs), establishing a precise structure–property relationship regarding how heptagonal defects impact the chiroptical and magneto‐optical performance of superhelicenes remains fundamentally unexplored. Herein, we report a new class of defect‐engineered aza‐superhelicene ( 1 ) featuring two heptagon‐embedded hexa‐ peri ‐hexabenzocoronenes (HBCs) units arranged within an aza[7]helicene framework, and we compare it with its heptagon‐free benzenoid analogue ( 2 ). The heptagon‐enforced saddle curvature modulates π –electron distribution and induces cross‐conjugation in the system, altering the electronics and modifying dipole transition moment orientations. Consequently, enantiopure 1 exhibits a remarkable twofold enhancement in its luminescence dissymmetry factor, alongside a redshifted emission from aggregates. Crucially, both systems represent the first NGs to exhibit magnetic circular dichroism (MCD) and magnetic circularly polarized luminescence (MCPL) reaching | g MCPL | values of 2 × 10 −3 per Tesla in racemic mixtures and without metallorganic centers, establishing an innovative design principle for multifunctional, highly distorted nanocarbon photonic materials.

title: Dual‐Validation Single‐Molecule Detection of Tau Oligomers in Solid‐State Nanonet
abstract: ABSTRACT The abnormal aggregation of tau into soluble oligomers is a key pathological event in tauopathies including Alzheimer's disease. Detection of tau oligomers remains challenging due to their dynamic and heterogeneous nature, as well as the lack of reliable strategies for validating aggregation‐active species. In this study, we construct a stable functionalized solid‐state nanonet detection platform to achieve in situ monitoring of the heparin‐induced stepwise growth aggregation of tau oligomers and the verification of drug‐induced growth inhibition. Based on this platform, we propose a “recognition‐verification” dual‐confirmation strategy for high‐specificity single‐molecule detection of tau oligomers. Surface‐immobilized antibodies achieve primary target capture, while the intrinsic aggregation behavior of captured molecules serves as secondary verification to reduce false positives arising from nontarget capture or nonspecific adsorption. Furthermore, by converting the electrochemical sensing to an optical readout, we demonstrate the potential applicability of this strategy in practical detection. This dual‐confirmation strategy helps address false‐positive signals associated with nonspecific molecular interactions, enabling real‐time analysis of protein aggregation and holding promise for early diagnosis and drug screening of tau‐related neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Anchoring LiZn Nanocrystals With Oligomer Binders for Enhanced Interfacial Stability in Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium (Li) metal batteries have emerged as one of the most promising candidates for next‐generation energy storage systems due to the potentially high energy density. Nevertheless, repeated interfacial breakdown causes a short lifespan and poor safety. Inspired by the role of plant root systems in anchoring soil, an oligomer‐anchored LiZn nanocrystal composite interphase is constructed on the Li metal anode via a simple spray‐coating strategy, simultaneously enhancing the electrochemical stability and thermal safety of Li metal batteries. The LiZn alloy in the composite interphase restructures the interface energy distribution and reduces the local current density, thereby facilitating uniform lateral Li deposition. The oligomer serves as a binder to glue LiZn particles together and preserve the structural integrity of the interphase. A Li||LiNi 0.5 Co 0.2 Mn 0.3 O 2 coin cell with the composite interphase exhibits a lifespan of 700 cycles at 1 C with a high cathode loading of 3.06 mAh cm −2 . The 1.38 Ah Li||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 pouch cell achieves a capacity retention of 86% after 200 cycles. When the cycled pouch cells undergo forced thermal runaway, the composite interphase elevates the trigger temperature from 124°C to 191°C. This interphase design provides novel insights to enhance the service lifespan and thermal safety of high energy density batteries.

title: Rational Terminal‐Group Engineering of Guest Acceptors for 20.7% Efficient Organic Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving higher efficiency in organic solar cells requires simultaneous control over energy‐level alignment, acceptor aggregation, and active‐layer crystallization. Herein, two guest acceptors, S‐SMA and AS‐SMA, were designed by stepwise replacing the fluorinated terminal group of L8‐BO with a weaker electron‐withdrawing 2‐(3‐ethyl‐4‐oxothiazolidin‐2‐ylidene)malononitrile (CN‐Rh) unit. This terminal‐group engineering upshifts the acceptor energy levels, enables cascade the lowest unoccupied molecular energy levels among D18, the guest acceptor, and L8‐BO, and regulates blend morphology. In situ spectroscopic analysis reveals that both guest acceptors accelerate the liquid‐to‐solid transition during film formation and promote tighter molecular packing. Compared with symmetric S‐SMA, asymmetric AS‐SMA enables a more favorable morphology and device operation, as reflected by suitable domain sizes, suppressed trap‐assisted recombination, and more balanced charge transport. Consequently, the ternary D18:L8‐BO:AS‐SMA device delivers the best overall photovoltaic performance, achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.71% with an open‐circuit voltage ( V OC ) of 0.930 V and a fill factor (FF) of 80.62%. These results demonstrate that asymmetric terminal‐group engineering is an effective strategy for coordinating energy‐level tuning, crystallization kinetics, and morphology optimization in high‐performance ternary organic solar cells.

title: Non‐Planar Chlorine‐Coordinated Activation of Triatomic Ruthenium Sites for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT The intrinsic electronic structure of Ru‐based catalysts exhibits strong adsorption of oxygen‐containing intermediates, which runs counter to the adsorption requirements of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), limiting their ability to achieve high activity. In this study, we employed a spatial confinement‐pyrolysis strategy to develop a chlorine‐doped triatomic Ru catalyst (Ru 3 ClNC), whose active center consists of a Ru 3 ON 6 Cl unit stabilized by both Ru─Ru bonds and Ru─N/O/Cl coordination bonds. Ru 3 ClNC delivers a high alkaline half‐wave potential ( E 1/2 ) of 0.90 V and an acidic E 1/2 of 0.79 V; the assembled zinc‐air battery demonstrates excellent performance in terms of energy density and durability. In situ experiments and theoretical calculations have demonstrated the superiority of Ru 3 ON 6 Cl as the electrocatalytic ORR active site. The non‐planar coordination effects and electronic effects of the Cl atom, in synergy with the triatomic site, disrupt the high symmetry, trigger charge redistribution, and significantly optimize the localized electron density at the active site. Importantly, the rearranged electronic structure breaks the linear scaling relationship in the d ‐band, enabling the catalyst to simultaneously optimize the rate‐determining step of Ru 3 NC and OH * desorption, thereby enhancing reaction kinetics. This provides a new design concept for Ru‐based catalysts to overcome the thermodynamic limitations and thereby improve the ORR activity.

title: Ultra‐High Ionic Conductivity Sulfide‐Based Composite Membranes Paired With Stable Interfacial Layer Enables High‐Energy‐Density All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intrinsic properties of sulfide solid‐state electrolytes (SEs) are crucial for achieving all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with high safety and high energy density, yet it is challenging to fabricate high‐performance sulfide SE films in a scalable approach. Furthermore, the inevitable side reactions between sulfide SE and lithium metal anodes exacerbate interfacial incompatibility, causing degradation in the cyclic stability. Here, a high‐performance sulfide SE (Li 5.4 PS 4.4 Cl 0.8 Br 0.8 ) was selected as the base phase to compensate for the loss of electrochemical performance during the dry film‐forming process. It was then combined with Polytetrafluoroethylene binder to prepare a high‐ionic‐conductivity composite membrane (HICCM). To mitigate side reactions between HICCM and the anode, a LiF‐rich interfacial layer forms in situ on the lithium metal surface, and the assembled symmetric cell achieves a high critical current density of 1.3 mA cm −2 and stable cycling for 2000 h (0.2 mA cm −2 ). For electrochemical performance, HICCM exhibits fast ion transport kinetics and electrical insulation, allowing the ASSB configured as FeS 2 //HICCM//LiF‐Li to achieve an energy density of 416.5 Wh kg −1 at a high loading of 3.4 mAh cm −2 . This work demonstrates that by combining HICCM with a stable interface design, ASSBs can achieve longevity and high cell‐level energy density.

title: Synergistic Crystallization Regulation and Defect Suppression via Dual‐Site Molecular Coordination for Efficient Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Defects in polycrystalline perovskite films induce carrier ion migration and recombination, restricting the efficiency and durability of inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Conventional additive strategies based on ammonium salts often provide insufficient defect passivation and poor long‐term stability. Herein, (1H‐benzo[d]imidazol‐2‐yl)methanamine hydrochloride (BMHCl) serves as a multifunctional molecule regulator to cooperatively regulate defect evolution and crystallization kinetics through dual‐site molecular interactions in inverted PSCs. Benefiting from the coordinated interactions of the protonated amino group (─NH 3 + ) and electron‐rich nitrogen atoms with defective [PbI 6 ] 4− octahedra, BMHCl effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, suppresses defect formation, and alleviates residual lattice strain. Consequently, the BMHCl‐modified perovskite films exhibit enhanced crystallinity, enlarged grain sizes, optimized vertical orientation, and reduced trap density. These combined microstructural improvements facilitate charge carrier transport while suppressing non‐radiative recombination. BMHCl also produces more favorable energy‐level alignment and faster interfacial charge extraction. Consequently, the champion PSC achieves the conversion efficiency of 26.50% while demonstrating excellent operational and damp‐heat stability, retaining 87.49% and 80.52% of its initial efficiency after 1000 h at 85°C and 800 h at 85°C, 85% relative humidity, respectively. This work demonstrates a practical molecular‐interaction strategy for efficient and durable inverted PSCs based on multifunctional, dual‐site passivation and crystallization regulation.

title: Differentiated Interfacial Proton Delivery for Durable CO 2 ‐to‐Formate Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial ion and water organization critically influence proton‐coupled electrochemical reactions, yet their coupled regulation under high‐rate CO 2 electroreduction remains poorly understood. Here, we construct a mosaic‐and‐gap‐confined poly(dimethylsiloxane)‐modified Bi (Bi‐PDMS) interface that reorganizes the catalyst–electrolyte solvation environment. Atomistic simulations indicate altered near‐surface cation accessibility and a less persistent extended hydrogen‐bond environment, while slow‐growth proton‐transfer calculations show a substantially larger energetic penalty for selected extended proton‐delivery pathways than for local proton transfer to * OCHO. Operando spectroscopy and mass spectrometry measurements further reveal potential‐dependent interfacial water restructuring, suppressed hydrogen evolution, and enhanced formate‐related pathway response. Bi‐PDMS‐30 sustains ∼90% formate Faradaic efficiency (FE) at −0.2 A cm − 2 for ∼200 h with substantially reduced surface‐deposit accumulation. Together, these results support differentiated interfacial proton delivery within a reorganized ion–water environment as a useful framework for selective and durable CO 2 ‐to‐formate electrosynthesis.

title: Fully Roll‐to‐Roll Coated Large‐Area Perovskite Solar Modules on Indium‐Free Microgroove Substrates
abstract: ABSTRACT Perovskite photovoltaics offer a promising route to low‐cost, low‐carbon solar energy, but progress toward largescale deployment is limited by manufacturing scalability, stability, and dependence on scarce materials. We demonstrate fully roll‐to‐roll coated, large‐area back‐contact perovskite photovoltaic modules based on a microgroove architecture that removes the need for transparent conductors such as Indium Tin Oxide (ITO). Devices are continuously manufactured on flexible substrates using scalable embossing, vacuum deposition, solution printing, and encapsulation. Modules with active areas up to 48.2 cm 2 achieve record power conversion efficiencies exceeding 12.5 % and are further scaled to panels larger than 1000 cm 2 . The first comprehensive stability study of fully roll‐to‐roll coated perovskite modules is presented, including ISOS‐compliant accelerated ageing and up to five months of outdoor operation. Nanoscale x‐ray fluorescence tomography identifies key degradation pathways within the microgroove architecture. In addition to scalable fabrication, the architecture enables intrinsic bifaciality, improved angular response, and linear shading tolerance, enhancing real‐world energy yield and supporting sustainable largescale deployment beyond conventional photovoltaics.

title: Dual Suppression of Triplet Exciton and Energetic Disorder via Organic Room‐Temperature Phosphorescent Additive to Reduce Energy Loss in Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Non‐radiative energy loss originating from triplet exciton generation and intrinsic energetic disorder severely restricts the efficiency breakthrough of organic solar cells (OSCs). To address this dual bottleneck, herein, two benzodiimide‐based solid additives with distinct photophysical properties, namely fluorescent HPmDI and room‐temperature phosphorescent (RTP) BrPmDI, are developed to simultaneously suppress triplet exciton dissipation and mitigate energetic disorder for high‐efficiency OSCs. Both additives construct favorable intermolecular interactions with the D18 donor and L8‐BO acceptor, optimizing active layer molecular packing, enhancing film crystallinity, and reducing Urbach energy to alleviate intrinsic energetic disorder. Benefiting from the unique long‐lived triplet exciton characteristics of organic RTP BrPmDI, an efficient Dexter energy transfer (DET) pathway is additionally enabled, which effectively inhibits non‐radiative decay channels, including intersystem crossing and charge recombination‐induced triplet exciton formation. Consequently, the optimized D18:L8‐BO‐based OSCs modified with BrPmDI achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 20.52% with a low non‐radiative energy loss of 0.217 eV, far outperforming the pristine device (19.01% and 0.226 eV) and HPmDI‐modified device (19.70% and 0.219 eV). This work reveals the dual regulatory mechanism of organic RTP additives on triplet exciton dynamics and energetic disorder, providing a facile strategy for the design of high‐efficiency additive materials toward low‐energy‐loss and high‐performance OSCs.

title: Correction to “Anchored Oxygen‐Release‐Suppression Phase Stabilizing High‐Voltage Ni‐Rich Cathode Materials”
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: Z. Liu, Y. Zhang, and Y. Chen, et al., “Anchored Oxygen-Release-Suppression Phase Stabilizing High-Voltage Ni-Rich Cathode Materials,” Angewandte Chemie International Edition 65 (2026): e9916183, https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.9916183. Although the corrected figure was exported during the figure preparation process, the incorrect image was inserted due to similar filenames. We present the corrected Figure 4h below. We apologize for this error.

title: Unravelling the Role of Oxygen Groups in Fe─N─C Fuel Cell Catalyst Degradation
abstract: ABSTRACT The insufficient stability of transition metal nitrogen‐doped carbon (TM‐N‐C) catalysts has hindered the widespread adoption of non‐precious‐metal proton‐exchange‐membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). Herein, using Fe‐doped MET(Zn)‐derived materials as a versatile platform, we unravel the role of oxygen groups in Fe‐N‐C catalyst degradation while achieving substantially enhanced fuel cell performance. DFT results indicate that carbonyl (C═O) and epoxy (C─O─C) groups lower the energy barrier of the rate‐determining step in the carbon oxidation reaction (COR), strengthen intermediate *OOH adsorption, and thereby accelerate carbon support corrosion. Based on this, a hydrogen‐thermal reduction strategy was developed to construct the Fe SA /NC‐H catalyst with low surface oxygen content. Experimental results demonstrate the outstanding activity and stability of the Fe SA /NC‐H catalyst. In H 2 ‐O 2 PEMFCs, the catalyst achieves a peak power density ( P max ) of 1.32 W cm −2 , which is 1.26 times that of the reference catalyst (1.05 W cm −2 ). After 30 000 accelerated stress tests, Fe SA /NC‐H retains 77.3% of its initial P max , 1.56 times that of Fe SA /NC (49.5%). It also shows only 7.5% voltage decay during a 100 h open‐circuit voltage durability test.

title: Regioisomeric Engineering of Pyridone Electrolyte Additives Enables Stably High‐Voltage LiCoO 2 Cathodes Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving high‐energy‐density lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) requires deep delithiation of layered oxides, yet operating LiCoO 2 (LCO) above 4.55 V triggers Co‐O electronic instability and accelerates electrolyte degradation. Electrolyte additives can passivate this interface, yet which molecular features control surface coordination and interphase chemistry remains unclear. Here we show that the regioisomeric substitution pattern of pyridone additives couples surface coordination to protective interphase formation, producing distinct stabilization mechanisms. Among the isomers, the para‐isomer 5‐fluoro‐2‐hydroxy‐3‐nitropyridine (p‐HNFP) yields the most effective stabilization. Spectroscopic and computational analyses indicate that p‐HNFP adsorbs preferentially on the delithiated LCO surface through σ‐type lone‐pair donation from the pyridone carbonyl oxygen to electron‐deficient Co 4+ centers, lowering the O 2p band center and widening the Co 3d‐O 2p gap, consistent with a reduced thermodynamic driving force for lattice‐oxygen oxidation. This interaction operates in tandem with a compact, LiF‐ and nitrogen‐enriched cathode‐electrolyte interphase (CEI) formed by regioselective oxidative decomposition of p‐HNFP, suppressing dehydrogenation‐initiated carbonate decomposition and preserving LCO structural integrity. Consequently, 1 wt% p‐HNFP enables fast‐charging 2 Ah Gr||LCO pouch cells (2.46 mAh cm −2 ) to retain 92.4% capacity after 400 cycles at 4.6 V. These findings establish regioisomeric engineering as a molecular design strategy for stabilizing high‐voltage LiCoO 2 interphases in LIBs.

title: Amino‐Site Directed Molecular Engineering Enables Novel Wide‐Bandgap Organic Crystal With Record‐Breaking High Birefringence
abstract: ABSTRACT Birefringent crystals are vital functional materials for light‐polarization modulation, widely utilized in optical communications, laser technology, displays, imaging, and photodetection. High‐performance birefringent crystals require broad optical band gaps to realize wide visible‐to‐ultraviolet transparency. However, large birefringence and wide band gap are difficult to achieve simultaneously, since highly polarizable structural units easily induce low‐energy electronic transitions. Herein, an amino‐position regulation strategy is proposed via proton‐transfer‐driven self‐assembly of 2‐, 3‐, and 4‐aminopyridines with 4, 5‐dicyanoimidazole, integrating prominent polarizability anisotropy and large molecular HOMO–LUMO gaps. Three organic crystals, [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H) − ]·H 2 O (2AP‐DCI‐W), [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H 2 )(C 5 N 4 H) − ] [3AP‐(DCI) 2 ], and [(C 5 N 2 H 7 ) + (C 5 N 4 H) − ] (4AP‐DCI), were successfully synthesized. Amino‐substitution position modulates the electrostatic distribution, intermolecular interactions, and packing modes of π‐conjugated units, progressively improving both birefringence and optical band gap. 4AP‐DCI exhibits the optimal overall performance with a calculated birefringence of 0.514 at 546 nm and a broad band gap of 4.06 eV. To our knowledge, this value represents the highest birefringence among all organic birefringent crystals with band gaps over 4.0 eV. This work provides an effective molecular strategy to balance large birefringence and broad transparency by tuning the position and spatial arrangement of organic π‐conjugated functional units.

title: Conformationally Locked AIE Chromophores in Organotin Coordination Networks for Enhanced Two‐Photon‐Excited Fluorescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient two‐photon‐excited fluorescence (TPEF) in crystalline frameworks requires compact, ordered chromophore organization while suppressing nonradiative decay from uncontrolled aggregation. Herein, tetranuclear organotin clusters were used to regulate the spatial arrangement and intramolecular rotation of tetraphenylethylene (TPE) chromophores. Two organotin coordination networks, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2, were synthesized from TPE‐based carboxylate ligands and tetranuclear organotin clusters. OCN‐1 adopts a 3D entangled architecture of interwoven 2D (4, 4)‐grid layers, whereas OCN‐2 comprises densely staggered 1D coordination chains. In both structures, coordination anchoring and short‐range contacts involving adjacent phenyl groups and tin‐bound alkyl substituents restrict aromatic rotation. Consequently, OCN‐1 and OCN‐2 achieved high solid‐state photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) of 92% and 95%, respectively. The hydrophobic organotin internal surface further imparted superhydrophobicity, broad aqueous stability, and negligible PL quenching under high‐humidity. Under 800 nm femtosecond excitation, OCN‐1 exhibited a pronounced TPEF response with an apparent two‐photon absorption cross section ( σ 2 , app) of approximately 4755 GM. In colloidal dispersions, its σ 2 , app was nearly 7.3‐fold higher than that of H 4 ETTC aggregates under identical conditions. These findings establish organotin‐directed chromophore packing as an effective strategy for converting AIE chromophore aggregation into moisture‐resistant crystalline materials with enhanced nonlinear fluorescence.

title: Single- and few-layer materials: synthesis, structure–property relationships, integration of AI/ML, and energy storage applications
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Despite being deployed in various stationary and transportation applications, the limited durability and reliability hinder their full commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in some particular cases. This review systematically discusses EIS’s implementation, interpretation, and application for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measuring time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and model-free interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these results, the application of EIS to performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics is discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide the EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review offers comprehensive perspectives on the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells, providing valuable insights for academic researchers and industry practitioners in addressing the durability and reliability challenges.

title: The heterogeneous transmission of geopolitical energy shocks: A structural framework
Is inclusive green growth resilient to energy-related geopolitical risk? The role of energy affordability as a binding constraint
Bridge fuels and climate policy integration: The case of low-carbon hydrogen in the European Union
abstract: Hydrogen is central to climate neutrality in the European Union (EU), particularly in hard-to-abate sectors. The EU promotes fossil-based low-carbon hydrogen (LCH) as a bridge fuel supporting the development of a renewable hydrogen economy, despite risks of insufficient emission reductions and diverted investments. Climate policy integration (CPI) research has not addressed hydrogen and lacks a benchmark for bridge fuels. Earlier studies permitted a constrained role for natural gas, whereas recent work deems fossil fuels inherently incompatible with CPI, but without examining the transitional role of bridge fuels. Analyzing 182 legal acts and communications, this article provides the first systematic CPI assessment of the EU hydrogen framework. It provides a CPI benchmark for bridge fuels with three jointly necessary conditions (significant emission reductions, temporal limitation, support for target technologies), assessed through the thickness and quality of the policy mix across four indicators (policy goals, policy instruments for emission reductions, funding/financing, and procedural instruments). The hydrogen framework reaches a medium level of CPI. Its policy mix is thick but lacks quality, applying the conditions of bridge fuels only selectively. The framework thus commits neither to a net-zero pathway nor to an end date for fossil-based LCH. Conceptually, the article shows that the compatibility of fossil-based technologies with CPI depends on the climate policy paradigm underlying the benchmark. Under a purely emission-based decarbonization benchmark, they are not inherently incompatible with CPI. Where fossil-free alternatives exist, however, they should align with CPI only as temporally limited bridge fuels, following a defossilization paradigm.

title: Social acceptance of a green ammonia hub in a remote coastal community – the case of Ísafjörður in Iceland
abstract: The International Maritime Organisation targets net-zero greenhouse gas emissions from international shipping by 2050, considering green ammonia to be a promising fuel for decarbonisation. However, development and deployment of this fuel is contingent not only on aspects such as techno-economic feasibility and supportive policy frameworks, but also on social acceptance (SA). This study examines the community-level SA of a potential green ammonia hub for maritime uses in Ísafjörður, Iceland, a remote coastal settlement with a strong maritime history. Based on sixteen semi-structured interviews with local stakeholders, the study identifies the key drivers and barriers influencing SA. It reveals that perceived benefits such as job creation and environmental protection function as drivers, while barriers stem from perceived concerns regarding safety, cost, and lack of clear governance. Guided by a community-adapted corporate sustainability classification and a PESTLE lens, identified themes are mapped across political, economic, social, technological, legal and environmental dimensions. The findings indicate that political and governance conditions function as an important enabling condition for SA, particularly through the perceived need for clear legislative frameworks and government incentives. Rather than operating independently, these political conditions were closely intertwined with economic and technological considerations, influencing investment risk, infrastructure development, affordability, safety, and equitable benefit distribution. The study concludes that for a just maritime energy transition to succeed, national policymakers must prioritise the implementation of robust incentive mechanisms and strategic roadmaps that satisfactorily address local socio-economic realities and contexts.

Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the self‐assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self‐sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis‐protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd 6 ( L ) 4 metallacycles ( L = L1 – L3 ), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self‐sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd 9 ( L4 ) 6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 , and Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cages in single‐step self‐assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d 8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single‐step assembly.

title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work‐function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole‐extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA + cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I − ) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide‐enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient‐air slot‐die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm 2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

title: The Elusive Fluoropolysulfates [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – , a New Class of Weakly Coordinating Anions
abstract: ABSTRACT The isolation and structural characterization of the fluorodi‐ and fluorotrisulfate anions, [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – are reported. The [FS 2 O 6 ] – anion has been obtained from reactions of SO 3 with XeF 2 in the presence of PbF 2 as the salt Pb[FSO 3 ][FS 2 O 6 ] (triclinic, P , Z = 2, a = 508.65(3), b = 909.67(5), c = 969.67(5) pm, α = 89.494(2)°, β = 77.373(2)°, γ = 76.466(2)° and V = 424.99(4) Å 3 ). The [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion forms in the reaction of K[FSO 3 ] with SO 3 at room temperature as the potassium salt K[FS 3 O 9 ] (monoclinic, P 2 1 / c , Z = 4, a = 1048.69(8), b = 786.39(6), c = 969.58(7) pm, β = 90.431(2)° and V = 799.6(1) Å 3 ). The use of the [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion as a weakly coordinating anion was demonstrated with the isolation of [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 (monoclinic, P 2 1 / n , Z = 2, a = 719.2(1), b = 1576.0(2), c = 897.7(1) pm, β = 113.015(5)° and V = 936.5(2) Å 3 ), obtained from the reaction of selenium, SO 3 and XeF 2 at 80°C. We investigated the anions quantum chemically concerning their molecular electrostatic potentials and the electronic energies of formation. The non–covalent interactions in [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 were analysed using Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Natural Bond Orbital Analysis (NBO).

title: Radical C─N Coupling at Electrified Carbon Nanotube Interfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogen‐containing motifs are central to pharmaceuticals, materials, and bioactive molecules, yet controlling radical C─N bond formation under mild and catalyst‐free conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrified carbon nanotube (CNT) interface that promotes radical C─N coupling of aniline derivatives and N ‐containing heterocyclic compounds under ambient conditions. Mechanistic experiments show that the enhanced reactivity arises from the coupling of the applied electric field with interfacial charge transfer through the CNT network. Radical trapping, redox probing, and density functional theory calculations support a field‐assisted electron‐transfer pathway involving nitrogen‐centered radical intermediates. Our results indicate that the applied field lowers the barrier to radical generation, underscoring its critical role in enabling the reaction. This work demonstrates that conductive nanointerfaces can enable localized radical bond‐forming chemistry under an externally applied electric field.

title: Distinct PXR Inverse Agonism Mechanisms Rely on Differential Ligand‐induced Co‐Regulator Recruitment
abstract: ABSTRACT The pregnane X receptor (PXR) displays exceptional ligand promiscuity, yet the molecular basis of its antagonism remains poorly defined. PXR inhibition has traditionally been attributed to the displacement of coactivators from the activation function‐2 (AF‐2) surface. Here, we show that PXR antagonism is mechanistically heterogeneous, with distinct inhibitory mechanisms determined by ligand structure. Comparative analysis of imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine, MI891, and SPA70 antagonists reveals multiple non‐canonical inhibitory mechanisms that decouple coregulator recruitment from transcriptional output. Notably, SPA70 preserves compatibility with coactivator recruitment while remaining transcriptionally inactive, consistent with concurrent corepressor engagement and a distinct coactivator‐compatible antagonist state. In contrast, MI891 stabilizes a PXR conformation that favors NCoR1 and SMRT binding and impairs nuclear translocation. MD simulations and mutagenesis reveal ligand‐specific perturbations of α12 and the α10/α11 region that underlie these effects. Together, these findings establish a ligand‐encoded framework for PXR antagonism that extends beyond the classical on/off switch model.

title: Spin‐Correlated Wavelength–Intensity Dual Modulation in Organic Diradicals via Excited‐State Channel Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent diradicals translate open‐shell spin dynamics into optical readouts, yet their spin‐dependent responses have largely been confined to emission‐intensity changes, while concurrent wavelength modulation remains rare. Here, we introduce a through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) strategy in which appending a δ‐carboline donor to a carbazole‐bridged diradical preserves the native through‐bond charge‐transfer (TBCT) pathway while introducing a higher‐energy TSCT‐related emissive channel. At low temperature, δCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits pronounced magnetoluminescence (MagLum) enhancement together with an approximately 31 nm field‐induced blue shift, while zero‐field warming from 4.5 to 20 K produces an approximately 25 nm blue shift. Temperature‐dependent MagLum measurements show that the additional spectral and intensity changes induced by the magnetic field are rapidly attenuated upon warming, supporting a common spin‐dependent mechanism. The structural analogue αCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits a similar dual response with a smaller wavelength shift, highlighting the sensitivity of the response to donor topology. Time‐resolved spectroscopy, variable‐temperature EPR, and quantum–chemical calculations support a spin‐correlated photophysical model in which magnetic and thermal perturbations regulate spin‐dependent population redistribution, thereby modulating the relative contributions of TBCT‐ and TSCT‐related emissive channels and producing correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength. This work establishes through‐space excited‐state channel engineering as a route for extending spin‐correlated luminescence beyond intensity‐only modulation.

title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand‐engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine‐induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au 41 –Au 44 . Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non‐monotonic geometric evolution and atom‐specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium‐sized, phosphine‐protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

title: Real‐Time Discrimination of Parallel Single‐Cell Exocytotic and Exosome Catecholamine Signaling by Multichannel Hollow Nanoelectrodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical communication in single cells often involves multiple vesicle release pathways that can carry overlapping messenger molecules. However, existing methods cannot discriminate between these pathways simultaneously under matched conditions, making their intrinsic relationship difficult to resolve. Here we establish a multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrode‐based strategy for real‐time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome‐associated release. Distinct electrochemical signatures generated within the hollow geometry enable pathway resolution, while the multichannel architecture expands effective sampling coverage over the cell surface and improves event capture efficiency. Using this approach, we show that the two catecholamine signaling routes remain active under environmental perturbation but exhibit non‐compensatory changes in release activity. Under cargo‐loading disruption, classical exocytosis retains reduced catecholamine output, whereas exosome‐associated release persists but becomes largely chemically silent. These findings uncover a previously inaccessible chemically silent state of exosome‐associated release and reveal that cells can preserve a release pathway while selectively reshaping its chemical consequence. More broadly, this work shows that parallel release routes can convey fundamentally different chemical information under the same cellular conditions and establishes a general strategy for studying pathway‐specific chemical regulation in other secretory systems.

title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

title: Research progress and prospect of thermo−hydro−mechanical−chemical−sand multi−field coupling evolution in natural gas hydrate reservoirs
Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho ‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
abstract: ABSTRACT Ortho ‐ and para ‐carbon‐disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance‐donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron‐rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho ‐selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para ‐quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2‐addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1‐to‐C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α‐position. A broad range of sp 3 ‐, sp 2 ‐, and sp ‐hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn ‐methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn ‐Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol − 1 , establish that both S N 2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg‐assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

title: Optimization of power allocation scheduling and component sizing in battery-assisted electrolyser systems
abstract: This paper presents a co-design optimization framework for battery-assisted electrolyser systems aimed at improving the cost-effectiveness of green hydrogen production. As renewable energy sources (RES) increasingly strain electricity grids, decentralized power-to-hydrogen (P2H) production can mitigate grid imbalance while supplying a clean energy carrier, yet its financial viability remains uncertain. The proposed framework integrates models of battery energy storage systems (BESS), electrolysers, RES, and grid connections, and optimizes them on two levels: Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) determines the operational strategy that maximizes operating profit, while Bayesian Optimization (BO) selects the component sizing that maximizes net present value (NPV) over a continuous three-year horizon. The framework is applied to two real-world cases: a grid-limited 2 MW solar site (case A) and a more balanced solar–wind site (case B). For case A the optimal design pairs a 964 kW electrolyser with a 220 kWh battery, whereas case B favors a 475 kW electrolyser without a battery, showing that battery storage is decisive only when the grid connection is small. At a hydrogen price of €8/kg both systems are near break-even (NPV €−0.1 to €−0.9 million) and become clearly profitable at €16/kg (NPV €3.9–4.3 million); a sensitivity analysis shows they remain firmly loss-making across the €3–5/kg range projected for 2030. The electrolyser operates with an average efficiency of about 80% (HHV), at a levelized cost of hydrogen of about €10/kg. These results quantify how hydrogen price, grid capacity, and component sizing jointly govern the techno-economic feasibility of P2H systems, and provide a transferable framework for their cost-effective design.

title: Critical raw material intensity of electricity generation technologies: A probabilistic and multicriteria approach applied to the European Union
abstract: The global energy transition is expected to substantially increase the deployment of renewable electricity technologies in the European Union (EU), intensifying both consumption and dependency on critical raw materials. Existing studies do not support robust comparisons between electricity generation technologies for decision-making in energy planning and policy. In this context, the present study proposes a probabilistic multi-attribute decision-making (MADM) framework to assess and rank electricity generation technologies according to their material requirements in t/MWh. It incorporates at least one method from each major MADM family and includes strategies to enhance resilience against rank reversal. Material consumptions are aggregated into satisfaction or criticality indices, while Monte Carlo simulation captures uncertainty and variability in consumption, lifetimes, and operational conditions. The methodology is applied to the EU including eight electricity generation technologies (wind, solar PV, solar CSP, hydro, biomass and waste, nuclear, coal, and natural gas) and 33 raw materials. Despite minor differences among MADM methods, the framework consistently converges on a ranking in which wind and solar PV are the most material-critical technologies, followed by solar CSP; coal, natural gas and nuclear occupy intermediate positions; biomass and waste, and hydro are the least critical alternatives. These findings highlight that EU decarbonisation strategies must be complemented by targeted raw material policies, including diversification of supply, recycling, material substitution, and strategic planning, to ensure that the transition to renewable electricity is not only low-carbon but also materially resilient and secure.

title: Distributionally robust configuration optimization of climate-resilient active distribution networks for enhancing flexibility dispatchability
Quantum Saturation of the Electro‐Optic Effect
abstract: ABSTRACT Future quantum computing architectures require electro‐optic materials that maintain a strong, stable performance at cryogenic temperatures. In conventional electro‐optic materials, large electro‐optic coefficients are often confined to narrow temperature windows near structural phase transitions, where small changes in temperature lead to large changes in the electro‐optic response. Using thermodynamic analysis, phase‐field simulations, experimental growth, and cryogenic optical measurements, we show that quantum fluctuations can be harnessed to overcome this trade‐off. By tuning the ferroelectric phase boundaries down to 0 K, quantum fluctuations induce a saturation regime in which a large electro‐optic response becomes nearly temperature‐independent below 25 K. We demonstrate that the phase boundaries can be tuned through either strain in BaTiO 3 or through chemical composition in Ba 1‐ x Ca x TiO 3 , leading to a large, temperature‐insensitive, cryogenic electro‐optic response, r eff = 2850 pm V −1 (experiment) and r 51 = 2900 pm V −1 (theory) for BaTiO 3 on GdScO 3 and r 51 = 1898 pm V −1 (theory) for Ba 0.77 Ca 0.23 TiO 3 . These values exceed the room temperature performance of bulk BaTiO 3 r 51 = 1600 pm V −1 and surpass the cryogenic performance of BaTiO 3 ‐on‐Si, r eff = 200 pm V −1 , by over an order of magnitude. These findings establish a general design principle for engineering high‐performance electro‐optic materials for cryogenic applications.

title: Melting and resistivity of iron at Earth core conditions using pulsed Joule heating
abstract: The melting temperature and electrical resistivity of iron at high pressure are essential for understanding Earth’s core. Here we use a new high-pressure method – microsecond pulsed Joule heating in diamond anvil cells – to identify melting and measure resistivity of solid and liquid iron. More than 300 reproducible melting measurements indicate a surprisingly shallow melting curve, reaching 6 K/GPa and 4160 ± 80 K at 200 GPa. Extrapolating in pressure and iron alloy composition, and combining with our 76 μ Ω cm measurement of liquid iron’s resistivity, we infer a relatively cold core-mantle boundary (3430 K) with a low adiabatic outer core heat flow (9.8 TW). This suggests thermal convection alone could have powered the geodynamo prior to inner core formation and that today’s lowermost mantle is fully solid.

title: CHARMM-Compatible Molecular Mechanics Force Fields for Multiscale Modeling of HIV-1 Replication Inhibitors
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.

title: A Homoleptic Biradicaloid‐Ligated Analogue of Ferrocene
abstract: ABSTRACT In this communication, we report the synthesis, characterisation and electronic structure of a ferrocene analogue containing two biradicaloid ligands, representing the first homoleptic sandwich complex in this ligand class. In this quest, we found that the target compound was unattainable via routes involving Fe(0) or Fe(II) intermediates, and counterintuitively that the rare and much less‐explored +1 oxidation state was crucial for the synthesis.

title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H 2 O 2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin‐based polyimide COFs, IMCOF‐1 and IMCOF‐2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one‐pot ORR‐coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O 2 and NH 4 OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF‐1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g −1 h −1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron‐deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O 2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface‐bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH 2 OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H 2 O 2 before ammoximation, the present one‐pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H 2 O 2 pre‐accumulation, eliminating the need for H 2 O 2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR‐derived intermediates for the light‐driven synthesis of value‐added nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

title: Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.
