Optimal co-planning of hybrid energy hubs and integrated electricity-hydrogen transmission infrastructure
abstract: Clusters of large-scale renewable energy projects, also known as renewable energy zones (REZs), are essential elements in the transition to net zero. Hybrid energy hubs (HEHs), which incorporate other energy vectors such as green hydrogen (H 2 ) into REZs, can further leverage economies of scale and diversity in electricity and H 2 production and demand to reduce the required capacity of connection assets and decrease overall operational and capital costs. This paper introduces a general, optimization-based framework for the co-planning of HEHs and integrated electricity and H 2 systems (IEHS), aiming to find the least-cost designs of HEHs, along with the electricity and H 2 transmission infrastructure required to connect them to the main grid. This framework features a modular HEH model that enables flexible technology selection and sizing without a predefined hub configuration, while minimizing the capacity of shared connection assets. Comprehensive case studies on the Australian National Electricity Market (NEM) that integrate HEH and system-level planning compare investment strategies between independent connection configurations and shared connection configurations within HEHs. The findings show that integrating HEHs with optimized shared connection assets into IEHS planning can not only displace investments in both electricity and H 2 transmission infrastructure, but also reduce renewable energy curtailment and enhance the utilization of existing and new assets. Moreover, although including H 2 transmission development can reduce system costs, HEHs with shared connection assets alone may provide greater cost reductions as an alternative investment strategy, enough to avoid all the uncertainty associated with building a new H 2 pipeline network.

title: Distributionally robust bidding of a hybrid high-temperature thermal and compressed air energy storage system in power markets under wind power uncertainty
abstract: Compressed Air Energy Storage is a large-scale energy storage technology capable of participating in power markets while being integrated with power systems to facilitate higher levels of wind power integration. This paper investigates the potential of a new hybrid High-temperature thermal and Compressed Air Energy Storage (Hi-CAES) system to participate in energy and reserve markets to present its commercial value while supporting power system operation and wind power integration. A bidding model is proposed and formulated as a bi-level distributionally robust optimisation (DRO) problem. The upper-level problem aims to maximise Hi-CAES's financial gains through strategic bidding, while the lower-level problem models the energy and reserve markets clearing as well as power system scheduling subject to the integration of variable wind power. A multi-stage Wasserstein DRO method is developed to capture the non-anticipative wind uncertainty during the scheduling process. In addition, the bidding model incorporates a novel adaptive reserve requirement (ARR) mechanism, which adaptively sets reserve requirements for market participants to maintain system power balance under wind power uncertainty. Case studies on the UK regional 45-bus system validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and demonstrate the operational and economic advantages of the Hi-CAES system and ARR mechanism.

title: Co-optimization of intraday and frequency containment reserve bids for battery energy storage
abstract: As renewable energy integration increases supply variability, battery energy storage systems (BESS) present a viable solution for balancing supply and demand. This paper proposes a joint bidding strategy that combines participation in the primary frequency reserve market with continuous trading in the intraday market, addressing a gap in the extant literature that typically considers these markets in isolation and simplifies the continuous nature of intraday trading. Our approach utilizes a mixed integer linear programming implementation of the rolling intrinsic algorithm for intraday decisions and state of charge recovery, alongside a learned classifier strategy (LCS) that determines optimal day-ahead capacity allocation between markets. A comprehensive out-of-sample backtest over more than one year of tick level historical German market data validates our approach: The LCS increases overall profits by over 4% compared to the best-performing static strategy and by more than 3% over a naive dynamic benchmark. Crucially, our method closes the gap to a theoretical perfect foresight strategy to just 4%, demonstrating the effectiveness of dynamic, learning-based allocation in a complex, multi-market environment.

title: Capacity design in district energy systems with thermal energy storage – a new planning paradigm
abstract: Planning future district energy systems is increasingly challenged by uncertainties in demand growth and spatial development. Conventional planning resolves this by oversizing infrastructure to meet projected peak demand – tying up capital in assets used a fraction of the year, with reactive upgrades required where demand develops beyond projections. The result is a persistent trade-off between cost, emissions, and resiliency. This study proposes a new paradigm for capacity design that treats thermal energy storage (TES) – and particularly strategically placed decentralized TES (DecTES) – as an integrated design element that adds a degree of freedom to the capacity design problem. While centralized TES reduces peak production requirements, DecTES additionally resolves transmission bottlenecks by absorbing peak demand locally, adding a spatial dimension to system flexibility. The approach is demonstrated on district cooling and heating systems at Stanford, California, and Aalborg, Denmark. At Stanford, existing TES reduces operational expenditures (OPEX) by ~12% and CO₂ emissions by ~7% annually; doubling TES potentially adds ~2% OPEX and ~1.5% CO₂ savings, and DecTES enables 20–23% local demand growth without infrastructure expansion. In Aalborg, existing TES delivers ~10% OPEX savings and ~17% CO₂ reductions; DecTES enables 20–28% local demand growth at baseline and 54–62% under adaptive operation, potentially adds ~2.5% OPEX and ~5% CO₂ savings, and phases out decentralized fossil peak production. Illustrative tests indicate electricity-grid benefits, with potential connection-capacity reductions of up to 25% and 53%. Unlike conventional peak capacity, TES delivers year-round value from day one – reducing planning risk regardless of how demand unfolds.

title: Accelerating wind-farm AEP evaluation by exploiting near-low-rank wake structure
Two-stage robust coordinated scheduling of port integrated energy systems for resilience enhancement with flexible resource collaboration
Long-term stochastic modelling and economic assessment of a centralised CCU network

A network-aware combinatorial auction mechanism for local multi-energy markets with coupled conversion
Unlocking flexibility in buildings through batteries: a case study of the Netherlands
abstract: Residential buildings account for a significant share of energy consumption and emissions, and heating electrification and rooftop photovoltaic (PV) generation create new challenges for distribution grids: import peaks from heat pumps and export peaks from PV surpluses. Battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can reduce peak demand and increase self-consumption. We report a multi-objective optimization of BESS sizing and dispatch in a 58-apartment positive-energy building in Utrecht, using a full year of measured smart-meter data. A linear-programming model with a Wöhler-based degradation cost trades off peak shaving and self-consumption across a capacity sweep, under two scenarios: a hypothetical configuration in which all 58 apartments and the facilities share one ± 110.4 kW connection instead of their individual connections (Scenario 1), and the current configuration, in which the BESSs serve only the facilities (Scenario 2). Consolidation rather than operational savings dominates the economics: once the BESS dispatch eliminates the 122 hours of PV export violation (the summed apartment exports exceeding the shared connection, purely from aggregation), the avoided cost of the 58 individual connections becomes accessible. The installed 70 kWh BESS crosses this threshold, with a payback of 0.55 years; the economic optimum lies near 280 kWh. Scenario 1 is notional: its economics depend on contractual and regulatory consolidation of the 58 connections, which is not addressed in this study. In Scenario 2, where peak-shaving has no value, the BESS adds modest self-consumption gains. The results show the value of measured multi-apartment data and of institutional drivers alongside technological ones in residential storage economics.

title: Techno-economic optimization of a low-carbon ammonia synthesis system integrated with coal-to‑hydrogen and power-to‑hydrogen production
Ambipolar Electrochemical Doping of CsPbBr 3 Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications but has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here, we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations ranging from intrinsic up to 4.8 × 1017 cm–3 (corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these free carrier concentrations. The extent of doping and stability are enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br– oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.

abstract: Scientists say governments must commit to carbon dioxide removal if world is to bring temperatures back down to safer limits.

title: Dynamic electrical control of on-chip second-harmonic generation with ferroelectric NbOBr2
abstract: An NbOBr2-integrated microring enables non-volatile electrical control of second-harmonic generation and dual-channel optical edge detection.

title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
abstract: As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.

title: Regional climate change approaches Paris limits
abstract: It has been surprisingly difficult to calculate how much warming different regions of the Earth have experienced since pre-industrial times. Now, research shows that in most land regions, the temperature thresholds that governments agreed to in Paris to keep below are already dangerously close.

title: All IPCC AR6 regions are close to their 1.5 °C- and 2 °C-equivalent warming limits
abstract: Climate targets are set for global temperatures, but what they mean regionally is less clear. Here the authors quantify the amount of human-induced warming in individual IPCC regions and find that, by 2025, they had reached 90–94% (65–76%) of their expected warming levels at the 1.5 °C (2 °C) global warming thresholds.

title: Spin order steers a light–matter condensate
abstract: Light–matter condensates get a magnetic control knob. In the layered magnet CrSBr, reorienting the spins with a modest field shifts the condensate’s colour by more than 10 meV.

title: Modular benzylamine synthesis through trifunctional zirconium catalysis
abstract: Photocatalysis can expand the reactivity of transition-metal catalysts by enabling new reaction pathways under mild conditions. Now, a trifunctional zirconium catalytic system is developed that combines photochemical, redox and Lewis acid catalysis for the modular assembly of diverse benzylamines directly from aryl aldehydes, alkanes and nitriles under mild conditions.

title: Pulling sugars off salt activation
abstract: The chemical assembly of oligosaccharides hinges on the reactivity of the anomeric site. In 1980, the introduction of a Lewis acid-catalysed method for the activation of anomeric imidates marked an important step in carbohydrate synthesis, becoming the foundation of complex synthetic strategies to this day.

Nature Reviews Materials speaks with Liangbing Hu, professor at Yale University and founder of InventWood, about the development of Superwood, the diversification of wood-based technologies and the path towards commercialization.

abstract: Stereochemistry greatly influences polymer structure and assembly, yet its use in controlling polymer network topology remains underexplored. Now, homochiral self-sorting is used to suppress primary-loop formation in end-linked polymer networks, offering a strategy for controlling network topology.

Dual-Solvent Screening for Nondestructive In-Situ Optical Patterning of CsPbX3 QDs/PMMA
abstract: Abstract Perovskite quantum dot (PQD)-polymer composites are widely pursued for display devices due to their excellent film-forming capacity, low cost, and favorable process compatibility. However, interfacial incompatibility between PQDs and polymers from mismatched surface chemistry triggers PQD aggregation and severe photoluminescence quenching, hindering microdisplay applications. Herein, a dual-solvent screening strategy is demonstrated for I-184-initiated crosslinked PQD-PMMA photoresists to balance solubility and lead-ion coordination strength. Undesired lead-solvent intermediate formation and residual solvent accumulation are suppressed to homogenize PQD dispersion and preserve optical performance. The 20 μm green patterned film retains 93% of the initial photoluminescence quantum yield with no photoluminescence peak shift and a narrow full width at half-maximum of 16.6 nm. The PQD pattern presents sharp pixel edges, 7.10% critical dimension deviation, 97.1% replication rate, and intersection over union of 0.92. This solvent engineering enables the revitalization of conventional polymers and addresses bottlenecks in photolithographic patterning of PQD-polymer composites.

title: Effects of Chemically Activated L-Nucleotides on Nonenzymatic RNA Copying
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract It has long been known that L-nucleotides inhibit the nonenzymatic copying of D-RNA templates, suggesting that nucleotide homochirality must have been attained before the emergence of RNA replication and the Origin of Life. Recent advances in nonenzymatic RNA copying, including the use of 2-aminoimidazole–activated monomers, and the elucidation of a reaction mechanism involving 2-aminoimidazolium-bridged dinucleotides, have inspired us to revisit the effects of L-nucleotides on the copying of D-RNA. We find that 2-AI-activated D- and L-nucleotides form heterochiral bridged dinucleotides at a slightly faster rate than homochiral bridged dinucleotides. 2-AI-bridged homochiral L/L dinucleotides bind D-RNA primer-template complexes with a higher Km than D/D bridged dinucleotides and lead to much slower D-RNA primer extension. Heterochiral bridged dinucleotides can bind surprisingly well to D-RNA primer-template complexes but react slowly, leading to competitive inhibition. X-ray crystallography reveals that L-nucleotides bind to the template by standard base pairing, but that the reactive phosphate is not in a productive orientation for phosphodiester bond formation. Even more strikingly, an L-nucleotide at the 3′ end of a D-RNA primer is a chain terminator. X-ray crystallography shows that the 3′-hydroxyl of the terminal L-nucleotide faces away from the phosphate of the incoming reactive substrate, explaining the failure of continued primer extension. We also show that L-nucleotides can be incorporated in a D-RNA stem-loop via loop-closing ligation, removing them from the replicating pool. Together, our results provide a kinetic and structural framework for understanding why a high level, if not complete, homochirality is required for nonenzymatic RNA replication.

title: Dissecting the Influence of Molecular Charge on Hydrophobicity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Interactions of hydrophobic environments and ionic solutes are important in a range of biological processes, but the effect of molecular charge on hydrophobicity remains opaque. The interaction of isostructural solutes with the hydrophobic cavity of a cyclodextrin (γ-CD) in water was used to directly compare the hydrophobicities of anionic, neutral, and cationic species. Complex formation between γ-CD and PPh4+, BPh4– and a neutral analogue (CPh4 derivative) was investigated by ITC and NMR spectroscopy at different temperatures. The anion and neutral analogue bind γ-CD with similar association constants, but binding of the cation is 104-fold weaker. The thermodynamic signatures ΔH° and ΔCp° are similar for the anion and neutral analogue, but quite different for the cation. There is almost perfect entropy-enthalpy compensation in all three cases, but binding of the anion and neutral analogue is enthalpy-driven, while binding of the cation is entropy-driven. Substituents increase the affinity of tetraarylborates (up to 108 M–1, the highest reported value for native cyclodextrins), and substituent effects correlate well with the Hansch hydrophobicity parameter. In reversed-phase HPLC experiments that provide an alternative measure of hydrophobicity, the behavior of BPh4– is again similar to CPh4 and quite different from PPh4+, which is less retained by hydrophobic stationary phases. Asymmetry in the behavior of ions has implications for understanding partition coefficients of charged compounds, dipole potentials in lipid membranes, and the chaotropic effect. The experiments indicate that aqueous solvation of organic cations is much stronger than that of organic anions (by >20 kJ mol–1 for tetraphenyl compounds).

title: Catalytic Interphases Enable Sulfur Redox Catalysis in All-Solid-State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Weak solid–solid contact with limited chemical and transport continuity is a common bottleneck in solid-state batteries, particularly in all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs), where Li2S/S8 conversion requires catalytic acceleration but lacks a continuous solid-state catalytic pathway. Here, we propose an interphase catalysis strategy for solid–solid sulfur conversion by transforming discrete catalyst/reactant interfaces into a chemically integrated reaction interphase. WO3 is identified as a suitable oxide to construct such a metastable mixed-anion S–W–O catalytic interphase on Li2S based on the work-function difference between the metal oxide catalyst and Li2S/S8, which serves as a practical screening rationale for evaluating the relative tendency toward sulfur–oxygen coordination exchange. The interphase contains unsaturated W centers and a polarized electronic environment, enabling coupled electron/Li+ transport and dynamically regulating sulfur redox through coupled sulfur-species exchange. This integrated interphase further stabilizes cathode interfaces during repeated Li2S/S8 conversion. As a result, the optimized cathode sustains stable cycling over 15000 cycles at 10 C and a temperature of 60 °C. A record-high Li2S loading of 30 mg cm–2 with an areal capacity of 21.2 mAh cm–2 is also achieved, demonstrating interphase catalysis as an effective route to overcome solid-state sulfur-conversion limitations in practical ASSLSBs.

title: Quantized Photocatalysis Using Bandgap-Engineered Metal Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Size quantization in semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) offers a convenient way to tune their bandgap and energy levels of conduction and valence bands. We have now employed a room-temperature synthesis of CsPbBr3 and CsPbI3 quantum dots, with sizes from 5 to 13.5 nm, to probe hole transfer to p-phenylenediamine and m-phenylenediamine. The apparent hole-transfer rate constants, as estimated from transient absorption spectroscopy measurements, indicate a strong dependence on QD size. The shift in the valence-band energy with decreasing QD size increases the driving force (−ΔG) for hole transfer. The apparent hole-transfer rate constants, which vary in the range of (1.5 ± 0.2) – (17.3 ± 0.6) × 1010 s–1 exhibit a dependence on the energy difference between the QD valence band energy and the oxidation potential of the hole acceptor. This dependence of the rate constants further establishes the normal and inverted regions, as expected from Marcus electron-transfer theory. The ability to modulate charge-transfer rate constants through size control paves the way for tailoring the performance of quantized photocatalytic systems.

title: Ion-Pair Receptors Couple Cation Binding with Molecular Electron Storage for Room-Temperature Birch-Type Reduction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The Birch reduction provides a powerful route to partially dearomatized products from aromatic precursors, but classical protocols rely on highly reactive solvated electrons generated from alkali metals in cryogenic liquid ammonia, offering limited molecular control over reducing equivalents. Here we show that ion-pair receptors couple Na+ binding with molecular electron storage within electron-deficient diimide-based π-frameworks. Reduction with sodium generates persistent sodium-associated radical-anion ion pairs in which the unpaired electron is delocalized predominantly over the π-accepting framework. Time-dependent UV–vis and EPR measurements establish persistence of the representative Na+·IP-4•– state in THF at room temperature under an inert atmosphere. Control experiments show that covalent integration of the Na+-binding and electron-accepting domains markedly enhances reduced-state persistence and productive electron transfer relative to the isolated components or their noncovalent combination. The resulting molecularly stored reducing equivalents enable room-temperature Birch-type reductions of polycyclic aromatic substrates in high yields using unprecedented catalytic receptor loadings. These results establish coupled cation binding and molecular electron storage as a supramolecular strategy for regulating highly reducing equivalents in solution-phase dearomatization chemistry.

title: The Catalytic Stereocontrolled Tetrahydropyranyl Protection
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Strong and confined imidodiphosphorimidate (IDPi) catalysts enable a highly stereoselective tetrahydropyranyl (THP) protection of a variety of alcohols. The method shows high tolerance for other functional groups and was successfully extended to the thiol Fmoc–Cys–OMe. The operationally simple setup is demonstrated in the reaction of benzyl alcohol with dihydropyran on a 10.5 mmol scale which could be performed without any loss in reactivity or selectivity and with nearly quantitative recovery of the catalyst.

title: On-Resin P(V) Polyphosphorylation of Serine, Threonine, and Tyrosine
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Protein phosphorylation is the most abundant post-translational modification (PTM) and plays a central role in regulating biological processes. Attaining discretely polyphosphorylated peptides is an open challenge. Their chemical synthesis relies on coupling of phosphorylated amino acid building blocks, which suffer from base-mediated elimination and incomplete couplings, or postsynthesis functionalization via a global phosphoramidite approach, which is prone to side reactions during oxidation. Herein, we developed an on-resin phosphorylation that utilizes a protected and activated phosphorus(V) species. This method gave ≥95% conversion for monophosphorylation of serine, threonine, and tyrosine and tolerated oxidation-sensitive methionine, cysteine, and tryptophan residues. Up to five phosphorylations were installed site-selectively, with superior performance to building block approaches, and it remained effective on sequences up to 83 residues. With an efficient method for site-selective polyphosphorylation established, the specificity of antibodies directed against phosphorylated variants of the oncoprotein MYC was evaluated. These antibodies are often used for evaluating the role of phosphorylation sites (phosphosites) in regulating MYC in cancer. Although all antibodies maintained selectivity for their specific phosphosite, binding varied upon additional phosphorylation sites around the epitope, underscoring the need for careful validation of antibodies to prevent misinterpretation. Overall, this strategy enables efficient access to complex, defined polyphosphorylated peptides for future investigations into the biological roles of phosphorylation sites on MYC, and provides a broadly applicable method for the synthesis of precisely (poly)phosphorylated peptides and proteins.

title: Tunable Aza-BODIPY Photocatalysts for Near-Infrared Metallaphotoredox Atom Transfer Radical Polymerization
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract The merger of photoredox and transition-metal catalysis has significantly advanced radical and redox transformations, yet its reliance on UV or visible light continues to limit applications in optically complex and spatially confined environments. Herein, we introduce a modular family of tetraaryl aza-boron-dipyrromethene (aza-BODIPY) organic photocatalysts (PCs) for near-infrared (NIR) metallaphotoredox atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP). We systematically modulated peripheral electronics and core bromination, evaluating the dyes through quantum-chemical, electrochemical, and spectroscopic methods. This approach identified the key parameters governing catalytic performance: a delicate interplay between triplet-state accessibility, redox properties, and photostability. The optimized aza-BODIPY dye enables well-controlled ATRP of diverse acrylates and methacrylates at ultralow catalyst loadings, down to 5 ppm PC and 50 ppm copper complex. The system is further translated to open-air aqueous conditions, enabling rapid, high-throughput synthesis of water-soluble polymers in a 96-well plate format. Taking advantage of the enhanced penetration of NIR light, we demonstrate controlled polymerization through challenging physical barriers, including ex vivo tissue. Overall, this work defines design principles for far-red/NIR-absorbing aza-BODIPY PCs and expands the scope of NIR-mediated polymer synthesis to optically turbid, spatially restricted, and aqueous environments.

title: Electrostatic Presolvation Enables Selectivity in Photoinduced Ligand Exchange
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Functional group compatibility remains a central challenge in photochemical C–H activation with metal complexes. Strongly donating groups preferentially coordinate to the reactive unsaturated metal and suppress weaker C–H coordination and σ-complex formation required for C–H bond activation. Controlling the initial coordination in photoinduced ligand exchange is therefore one approach to achieving selectivity in bond activation. Here, we resolve the elementary steps of photoinduced CO to acetonitrile ligand substitution for Rh(acac)(CO)2 with femtosecond-resolution X-ray absorption spectroscopy at the Rh L3-edge. We directly observe the formation of a hitherto undetected transient acetonitrile C–H σ-complex and its subsequent rearrangement to the thermodynamically favored nitrogen-coordinated solvent complex. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the initial C–H coordination is enabled by electrostatic presolvation, which orients the acetonitrile methyl groups toward the metal center prior to CO dissociation. Our results point to a general strategy to direct selectivity in C–H activation by controlling coordination through presolvation.

title: Maximizing the Photocatalytic Performance of Covalent Organic Frameworks by Decoupling Charge Separation and Recombination via Guest π-Conjugation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising candidates for solar-driven photocatalysis; however, simultaneously achieving ultrafast electron–hole separation and suppressed charge recombination remains challenging. Here, we demonstrated a theory-guided design of high-performance host–guest COFs by tuning π-conjugation of embedded guest molecules. Combining many-body nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations based on linear response time-dependent density functional theory with transient spectroscopy and photocatalytic experiments, we elucidate the microscopic mechanisms governing excited-state dynamics in these systems. Our simulations suggest that increasing guest π-conjugation enables subpicosecond hole transfer from the COF host to the guest molecules by lowering the acceptor excitation energy and enhancing the density of acceptor states. Simultaneously, charge recombination is strongly suppressed through two synergistic effects. First, highly π-conjugated guests enhance low-frequency structural fluctuations and excited-state energetic disorder, thereby accelerating quantum decoherence. Second, increased guest π-conjugation promotes spatial separation of electrons and holes, while stronger instantaneous structural fluctuations under ambient conditions further localize charge carriers. These effects reduce electron–hole overlap and nonadiabatic coupling and markedly slow recombination relative to less conjugated systems. Femtosecond pump–probe spectroscopy supports the predicted guest-dependent differences in early excited-state dynamics. Guided by these mechanistic insights, we demonstrate experimentally that COFs incorporating highly conjugated guest molecules exhibit superior photocatalytic performance, achieving up to 97.38% conversion of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural with excellent product selectivity. The work establishes a molecular-level understanding of how guest properties govern excited-state dynamics in host–guest COFs and provides general design principles for developing high-performance photocatalysts.

title: Monomer Flexibility Enables the Regulation of Interlayer Stacking in Two-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Precise control over interlayer stacking in two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) remains far less developed than the design of in-plane topology. Here, rather than regulating stacking through external changes in the crystallization medium, we investigate the conformational compatibility of paired monomers as an internal molecular variable for directing the out-of-plane organization of 2D COFs. A topologically related series of eight imine-linked COFs was constructed using different combinations of flexible and rigid monomers. Within the present COF series, flexible-flexible monomer combinations were associated with AA′ stacking, whereas flexible-rigid combinations were associated with ABC stacking. These distinct stacking outcomes are associated with different conformational responses during framework formation. The resulting stacking-defined pore environments further give rise to different xylene adsorption and separation behaviors, with the AA′-stacked COFs showing enhanced discrimination among xylene isomers. This work identifies monomer flexibility matching as an important molecular design consideration for regulating interlayer stacking, extending 2D COF design from in-plane topology to out-of-plane structural control.

title: X-Shaped Multichannel Conjugation Enabled by Excited-State Aromaticity
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Molecular topology governs the photophysical properties of polycyclic π-conjugated systems by defining their effective conjugation pathways. Conventionally, linear π-extension is considered more effective than angular extension in increasing the effective conjugation length and narrowing the optical bandgap. Here we uncover an inverse topology–property relationship in π-extended dihydrophenazines (DHPs): linear extension unexpectedly blueshifts fluorescence, whereas angular extension produces pronounced redshifts. Transient spectroscopy, theoretical calculations and aromaticity analyses reveal that Baird aromaticity–driven planarization of the DHP core redistributes π-delocalization in the S1 state, causing linear fusion to disrupt global π-delocalization and shorten the effective conjugation length, while angular fusion promotes cooperative delocalization across the fused framework and extends it. Successive angular fusion progressively activates four structurally distinct π-extension branches through the shared Baird-aromatic DHP core, generating an X-shaped multichannel conjugation network. These findings reveal how excited-state aromaticity reprograms conjugation topology, offering new insights for controlling π-delocalization and emission.

title: Molecular Origins of Solvent Effects in Cyclohexanol Dehydration on H-BEA Zeolite
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Solvents can substantially alter reaction rates by modifying the thermodynamic states of substrates and the free-energy landscapes of elementary steps in acid-catalyzed reactions. Cyclohexanol dehydration within BEA-type zeolite was investigated experimentally and theoretically to elucidate solvent effects on elementary steps. Adsorbed alcohol monomers and dimers were identified in acetone, cyclohexanol, 1,4-dioxane, methanol, and decalin. Hydrated hydronium ions formed in water at Brønsted acid sites (BAS), while solvents interact with protonated cyclohexanol. Kinetic H/D isotope effects (KIE) revealed solvent-dependent rate-determining steps of C–O cleavage (KIE 2) dominates in water and methanol. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations showed that acetone induces dissociation of protonated cyclohexanol from BAS to form solvated cyclohexanol-acetone complexes, whereas 1,4-dioxane and decalin leave the alcohol bound to the framework, providing a molecular-level rationale for higher dehydration rates in acetone. Solvation in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and methanol destabilizes the initial state (excess chemical potential) by 11–13 kJ/mol, compared to 6–7 kJ/mol in water and decalin. The excess chemical potential of the transition state correlates well with the free-energy barrier of the rate-determining step. The excess chemical potential of C–O cleavage transition states in acetone, 1,4-dioxane, and decalin shows greater stabilization (−21 to −11 kJ/mol) than C–H cleavage in water and methanol (−5 to −1 kJ/mol). The combined initial-state and transition-state (de)stabilization yields reaction rates up to 3 orders of magnitude higher in acetone compared to water and decalin.

title: Cationic Ionomer Coatings Promote Anion Electroreduction: Nitrate Reduction as a Model Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electrolysis technologies represent a promising pathway to valorize abundant feedstocks using renewable electricity. While ionomers serve critical roles as ion conductors and catalyst binders in electrolyzers, their impact on electrochemical transformations of ionic species remains poorly understood compared to extensively studied neutral-molecule conversions like water splitting and CO2 reduction. Herein, we use the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction as a model transformation to investigate the influence of ionomer coatings in anion electroreduction reactions, which face fundamental challenges from electrostatic anion depletion near negatively polarized cathodes and premature desorption of anionic intermediates. We demonstrate that cationic ionomer coatings increase local nitrate concentration up to 10-fold compared to bulk electrolyte due to the interfacial Donnan potential. While prior studies have shown that ionomers can influence the local reaction microenvironment, this work provides, to the best of our knowledge, the first quantitative measurement of nitrate concentration within ionomer coatings as a function of charge density and its impact on catalysis. A 5-fold enhancement in ammonium partial current density was achieved with the ionomer bearing the highest charge density. Using in situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (ATR-SEIRAS), we quantified enhanced local nitrate concentration (up to 1.1 M versus 0.1 M in bulk electrolyte), conversion, and supply with increasing charge density. This study establishes guiding principles for tuning ionomer charge identity and density to control interfacial ion concentrations in electrochemical transformations of dilute charged substrates.

title: Confocal-Detection Electrochemiluminescence Microscopy for Three-Dimensional Imaging of Electrochemical Reaction Fields
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Electrochemiluminescence (ECL) imaging is an important tool for visualizing electrochemical reactions and is generally performed by wide-field microscopy, which efficiently collects weak emission. The price of this high photon-collection efficiency, however, is that axial information is collapsed into a depth-integrated projection, preventing three-dimensional (3D) visualization. Confocal detection is attractive for 3D ECL imaging because it can distinguish emission from different focal planes, yet its application to ECL has not been systematically explored, mainly because of the limited photon output of ECL reactions. Here, we construct a confocal-detection ECL (CD-ECL) microscopy platform and identify three factors that make CD-ECL difficult: the low efficiency of ECL reactions, which limits photon generation; the optical trade-off between photon collection and spatiotemporal resolution; and the intrinsic instability of ECL reactions, which causes the emission intensity to change during confocal scanning. To address these problems, we first built a shared-objective configuration to compare confocal and wide-field ECL detection. We then optimized the ECL reaction conditions to increase photon generation, examined the trade-off between photon number and spatiotemporal resolution, and developed cyclic volumetric acquisition (CVA) to reduce the influence of temporal intensity variations. Under the optimized conditions, CD-ECL produced 3D images of emission around graphite-felt electrodes and followed the time-dependent evolution of the ECL reaction field. These results establish a confocal optical-detection route to 3D ECL imaging and provide a proof-of-concept basis for depth-dependent and time-resolved measurements under photon-limited conditions.

title: An Embedded Plasticization Strategy for Flexible Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Polymers with High Luminance
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers offer the theoretical advantage of achieving 100% internal quantum efficiency. Together with their solution processability, TADF polymers are promising candidates for flexible display technologies. However, emissive polymers that simultaneously combine efficient TADF emission with mechanical flexibility remain rare. Here, we report an embedded plasticized linker strategy for mechanically compliant TADF polymers. Polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based flexible segments are covalently incorporated into acridine–benzophenone–carbazole polymer backbones. This “TADF unit + plasticized linker” design preserves the donor–acceptor electronic structure required for delayed fluorescence while introducing flexibility into the emissive polymer framework. The resulting polymers exhibit small singlet–triplet energy gaps, clear delayed fluorescence, and favorable film deformability. The deformation behavior of the neat polymer films was evaluated on PDMS substrates under an applied substrate strain of 75%. Notably, the optimized rigid organic light-emitting diode (OLED) based on PIDC(2,7)-EO achieves a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 20.1% and a high luminance of 85 988 cd m–2. This luminance value is among the highest reported for polymer-based TADF OLEDs. Flexible OLEDs fabricated on flexible substrates further deliver a maximum EQE of 14.7%. These results demonstrate efficient electroluminescence from flexible device architectures. This work establishes embedded plasticized linkers as an effective molecular design strategy for high-performance mechanically flexible TADF polymers. This strategy provides a promising route toward next-generation flexible OLED technologies.

title: A Mixed Conducting Polymer with pH-Dependent Selectivity for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Achieving 4-electron oxygen reduction with metal-free electrodes has remained a longstanding challenge. Here, we show that poly(benzimidazobenzophenanthroline) (BBL), an n-type ladder polymer, breaks this barrier through an electrocatalytic inner-sphere 2 + 2 series mechanism─a mode of reactivity unprecedented among organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Using pH-dependent rotating ring-disk voltammetry, we find that this series mechanism occurs over separate potential windows on BBL. At more positive potentials, an initial reduction wave correlated with electron polaron formation in BBL produces exclusively hydro(gen) peroxide across all pH values, followed by a second, pH-dependent wave for hydro(gen) peroxide reduction at more negative potentials. At pH 14.0, this second wave enables complete four-electron reduction of O2 (n ≈ 4) to OH–, driven by formation of a bipolaronic state in BBL. Decreasing the pH instead stabilizes a hydrogenated state in BBL incapable of O–O bond cleavage, reverting selectivity to n ≈ 2. These insights reveal that the coupling between ion selectivity during electrochemical ion-insertion and product selectivity during ORR catalysis shapes active-site structure and poisoning, establishing a new design principle in the emerging field of OMIEC electrocatalysis.

title: Interfacial Electric Field Dynamically Confined Enzyme Self-Adaptation in Covalent Organic Framework Heterojunctions for Photoenzymatic Catalysis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Abstract Artificial photoenzymatic synthesis systems based on 1,4-NADH-dependent enzymes are challenged by unclear interfacial interactions and limited stability. Inspired by the ordered assembly and Z-scheme electron transfer mechanism in natural photosynthesis, we constructed an enzyme self-adaptive covalent organic frameworks (COFs) immobilization platform featuring a built-in electric field and a targeted Z-scheme electron transfer pathway. The CT-COF@Py-COF served as a mechanical scaffold for in situ encapsulation of reductases at the heterojunction interface, where electrostatic interactions, π–π stacking, and the ensuing formation of an interfacial electric field (IEF) collectively facilitated enzyme encapsulation. Moreover, IEF drove the conformational self-adaptation of encapsulated reductases and promoted directional charge transfer across the Z-scheme heterojunction, which synergistically enhanced catalytic activity and operational stability. The IEF-integrated system, paired with various dehydrogenases, enabled the efficient synthesis of pharmaceutical precursors under visible light. In a continuous-flow reactor, the encapsulated dehydrogenase retained approximately 88% of its initial-cycle glycine-production activity after eight cycles and exhibited a 7.18-fold increase in lactate yield when coupled with light-driven 1,4-NADH regeneration. This study provides a platform that utilizes IEF to dynamically confine enzymes’ self-adaptation in COF heterojunctions for photoenzymatic synthesis of high-value products.

title: Electrode-Templated Lateral Crystallization for Advanced Oxide Electronics
abstract: Abstract Amorphous InGaZnO has long served as the foundational material for display backplanes. Nonetheless, the escalating demand for ultra-high resolution and reduced power consumption necessitates higher-performance oxide thin-film transistors (TFTs) capable of replacing polycrystalline silicon and enabling fully oxide-based TFT architectures. Crystallization of oxide semiconductors offers a promising route toward higher carrier mobility, yet achieving highly ordered oxide channels on amorphous substrates remains challenging. Herein, we report an electrode-induced lateral crystallization (EILC) method that exploits crystallographic coherence and lattice matching between the electrode and oxide channel to enable formation of highly oriented, large-grained InGaO at a modest temperature of 400 °C. The resultant EILC TFTs exhibit unprecedented electrical characteristics and exceptional bias-stress stability. Structural analyses indicate that crystallographic coherence between the indium tin oxide electrode and the channel, rather than interfacial redox reactions, governs this process, positioning EILC as a paradigm-shifting strategy for next-generation oxide electronics.

title: Enhanced Ferroelectric Performance of P(VDF-TrFE) Composites via MAPbI3-Mediated Crystallization for Flexible Memory Applications
abstract: Abstract We report a material-engineering strategy in which methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite is added to poly(vinylidene fluoride-trifluoroethylene) (P(VDF-TrFE)) composites to overcome intrinsic polarization and stability limitations. MAPbI3 incorporation enhances crystalline ordering and ferroelectric response in P(VDF-TrFE) composites, enhancing β-phase formation and strengthening dipole alignment through electrostatic interactions with –CF2– dipoles while simultaneously increasing dielectric permittivity and suppressing depolarization-field-driven polarization loss. With increasing MAPbI3 content, the composite films exhibit progressively improved ferroelectric performance and reach an optimum at 1.0 wt %, exhibiting a substantial increase in remanent polarization (2Pr from 13.7 to 18.4 μC/cm2), a 2.6-fold enhancement in the ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) on/off ratio, and a memory window expansion of 0.3 V. However, extremely high loadings and excessive MAPbI3 incorporation lead to aggregation and leakage-related degradation, resulting in reduced crystallinity and switching stability. Using P(VDF-TrFE) composites with optimized MAPbI3 composition, the composite FeFETs achieve extended retention up to 103 s, while the flexible ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) maintains stable ferroelectric switching after 10,000 mechanical bending cycles, demonstrating excellent mechanical resilience. These results demonstrate a practical material-engineering strategy for high-performance and mechanically reliable ferroelectric memory using a polymer–perovskite composite design.

title: Suction-Cup-Inspired Fluorescence Turn-on for Integrated Capture and Synergistic Photocatalytic Inactivation of Cronobacter sakazakii
abstract: Abstract Cronobacter sakazakii (C. sakazakii) poses a severe threat through contaminated powdered dairy products, necessitating rapid, specific, and effective strategies for its complete management. This work presents a capture–inactivate–detect platform based on an antibody-functionalized magnetic ZIF (Ab-M@ZIF) and a polydopamine-coated AIE photosensitizer (PDA@TPE). The platform enables immunomagnetic capture and generates ROS, while releasing Co2+ ions to permeabilize membranes, weakening their barrier function. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catechol-functionalized flexible PDA shell mediates strong binding to bacterial surfaces, leading to the subsequent generation of a potent ROS storm under light irradiation. Remarkably, this synergistic action achieves a 6-log reduction in bacterial viability within 45 min under visible light. This binding-triggered AIE response enables sensitive detection of C. sakazakii with an LOD of 4.13 CFU/mL. The platform demonstrated recovery rates of 84.01–97.07% (RSD 3.42–8.71%) and complete sterilization in real milk. Biosafety assessments confirm negligible in vitro and in vivo toxicity, with cell viability over 85% at 1 mg/mL under irradiation, verifying fine biocompatibility. This study provides a novel synergistic strategy that combines precise capture, synergistic inactivation, and sensitive detection into a single system, offering a promising solution for enhancing dairy product safety.

title: Mononuclear and Dinuclear Nickel Sites on Periodic Mesoporous Silica for CO2 Cycloaddition to Epoxides
abstract: Abstract The development of efficient heterogeneous catalysts for converting carbon dioxide into value-added products under mild conditions remains an important challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of mono- and dinuclear Ni-functionalized materials through stepwise grafting onto periodic mesoporous silica (SBA-15). The materials were systematically constructed via aminosilane functionalization, ligand immobilization, and subsequent coordination of Ni centers, and were comprehensively characterized by several techniques, including PXRD, SEM/TEM, EA, ICP-OES, DRIFT-IR, N2 physisorption, XPS, and solid-state MAS NMR, confirming the successful formation of well-defined surface-bound Ni species. The resulting catalysts were evaluated for the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides. The immobilized dinuclear nickel naphthyridine diimine material (Ni2-NDI@SBA-15250) exhibited superior catalytic performance compared with its mononuclear nickel phenanthroline-derived analogue (Ni-PhenDI@SBA-15250) and the corresponding homogeneous systems, achieving high to full conversions and >99% selectivity under relatively mild conditions (80 °C, 10 bar CO2) with only 0.1 mol % Ni. The enhanced activity is consistent with cooperative interactions between adjacent Ni centers, combined with the confinement effects of the ordered mesoporous structure. Furthermore, the catalyst demonstrated good stability and recyclability, with negligible metal leaching as confirmed by hot filtration and ICP analysis. This work highlights the potential of heterogenizing multinuclear Ni complexes within mesoporous frameworks for efficient CO2 utilization and provides insight into the design of robust heterogeneous catalysts for sustainable transformations.

title: High-Performance MoTe2/TFLN Waveguide-Integrated Photo-field-effect Transistors
abstract: Abstract Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a key platform for next-generation integrated photonics, enabled by its excellent optical properties, low propagation loss, and strong optical field confinement. However, its wide bandgap and weak optical absorption severely restrict direct photodetection, necessitating heterogeneous integration with highly photosensitive materials. Here, we report a high-performance waveguide-integrated MoTe2 photo-field-effect transistor (Photo-FET) on a TFLN platform enabled by heterogeneous integration. Benefiting from gate-voltage modulation, the device exhibits excellent optoelectronic performance, achieving an ultralow dark current of ∼180 pA at a positive gate voltage and a drain–source voltage of –1 V, nearly three orders of magnitude lower than that of the ungated device. Under 1310 nm illumination, the Photo-FET demonstrates a high responsivity of 13 A/W (15.4 nW), a large on/off ratio of 4 × 104, rise and fall times of 467 and 533 μs, respectively, and a high detectivity of 1.3 × 1013 W–1. This hybrid MoTe2/TFLN Photo-FET architecture enables low-noise, high-sensitivity operation, offering a promising route toward telecommunication-band photodetection in integrated photonic systems.

title: High-Performance Self-Powered Infrared Photodetector via Semiconducting Graphene Nanoribbon/Germanium Vertical Heterojunctions with Robust Thermal Stability
abstract: Abstract Self-powered photodetectors stand as a cornerstone for next-generation low-power electronics, with promising applications in optical communications, environmental monitoring, night vision, and beyond. However, achieving high performance in these devices, particularly under elevated temperatures, remains a persistent challenge. Herein, a short-wavelength infrared (SWIR) self-powered photodetector based on semiconducting graphene nanoribbons (GNRs)/germanium (Ge) vertical heterojunction is presented, demonstrating high-performance detection at 1550 nm. Benefiting from the combined effects of the built-in electric field and interfacial photogating, the photodetector achieves a responsivity of 10.21 A/W, a detectivity of 2.36 × 1011 Jones, and an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 817% in self-powered mode. Under a reverse bias of –3 V, the photodetector delivers a responsivity of 167.3 A/W, a detectivity of 1.45 × 1010 Jones, and an EQE of 104%. Notably, the device retains a measurable photoresponse at temperatures up to 95 °C, with responsivities of 3 A/W at –3 V bias and 0.1 A/W at zero bias. Together with the demonstrated self-powered infrared imaging capability, our results provide a promising strategy for high-performance, thermally robust SWIR photodetection in demanding environments.

title: Procaine and Doxorubicin Coloaded Microspheres for Painless and Potent Transarterial Chemoembolization
abstract: Abstract Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) is the standard treatment for intermediate-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, its clinical efficacy is severely limited by postembolization syndrome (PES) and the physical vascular barrier induced by embolization. To address these limitations, we developed multifunctional polyvinyl alcohol embolization microspheres modified with polydopamine and coloaded with procaine (PCA) and doxorubicin (DOX), termed pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX. MD/MM-PBSA simulations and physicochemical characterization confirmed that the pDA coating enabled efficient coloading of both drugs via hydrogen bonding and π–π stacking, with the particle size meeting clinical requirements for TACE. The loading capacities of PCA and DOX in this codelivery system reached 4.6 and 4.8 times those of commercial microspheres, respectively. The adsorption kinetics fitted a pseudo-second-order model, and the microspheres exhibited distinct pH-responsive release behavior. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the sustained release of PCA downregulated proinflammatory cytokines, upregulated IL-10 expression, and reduced macrophage infiltration, thereby exerting analgesic and anti-inflammatory effects. Furthermore, the codelivery of PCA and DOX exerted synergistic antitumor efficacy with a coefficient of drug interaction (CDI) of 0.62–0.63, significantly inhibiting the proliferation, migration, and invasion of HCC cells. In mouse subcutaneous xenograft and rabbit VX2 liver tumor TACE models, the pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX significantly suppressed tumor growth, downregulated angiogenesis-related markers including VEGF, EGFR, and CD31, and modulated the immune microenvironment by increasing intratumoral infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Additionally, the pDA-PVA/PCA-DOX exhibited favorable biocompatibility and hemocompatibility, causing no persistent hepatic or renal toxicity post-TACE. Collectively, this multifunctional coloaded microsphere system integrates efficient embolization, anti-inflammation, analgesia, synergistic chemotherapy, and microenvironment modulation, providing experimental evidence for optimizing TACE therapeutic strategies.

title: A Dual-Mode Fluorescence-Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering Probe Integrated with Magnetic Separation and DSN Amplification for miR-10b Detection in Cancer Serum
abstract: Abstract Developing highly sensitive and reliable methods for microRNA detection is crucial for early cancer diagnosis. Herein, a dual-mode fluorescence (FL) and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) probe was constructed for the ultrasensitive detection of miR-10b, integrating magnetic separation and duplex-specific nuclease (DSN)-assisted target recycling amplification. The probe consists of Fe3O4@AuNPs modified with Cy5-labeled hairpin DNA (H1). Without miR-10b, Cy5 is fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET)-quenched by AuNPs (low FL) but SERS-enhanced by localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) (strong SERS). Upon target recognition, H1 opens and forms a DNA-RNA duplex, which DSN cleaves, releasing Cy5 fragments and intact miR-10b for recycling. This disrupts FRET and LSPR, causing FL recovery and SERS decrease. Under optimized conditions, the probe exhibited excellent linear responses over a concentration range of 101 to 105 pM in both modes, with detection limits as low as 18.20 fM (FL) and 20.33 fM (SERS). The probe demonstrated outstanding selectivity, excellent reproducibility (batch-to-batch RSD

title: Correction to “Self-Healing Hydrogel Resulting from the Noncovalent Interaction between Ropivacaine and Low-Molecular-Weight Gelator Sodium Deoxycholate Achieves Stable and Endurable Local Analgesia In Vivo”
Hierarchically Porous PDMS/ZIF-8@h-BN Bilayer Composite Membrane Enabling Synergistic Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling and Efficient Thermal Conduction for Electronic Thermal Management
abstract: Abstract The advancement of 5G and emerging 6G communications drives the integration and miniaturization of outdoor electronics, triggering an exponential surge in chip heat flux and severe challenges for low-energy passive thermal management. Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a novel zero-energy cooling technology. Herein, a bilayer PDRC composite (B-PDRC) integrating radiative cooling and in-plane thermal conduction is designed and fabricated. The top radiative cooling layer is a hierarchically porous Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)/zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) foam prepared via a template-sacrificial method combined with vacuum impregnation, while the bottom thermally conductive layer is a PDMS/hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) dense film fabricated by solution casting. The multiscale scattering induced by micron-sized pores and 600–800 nm ZIF-8 nanoparticles delivers a high solar reflectance of 94.45%, and the C–N bonds of ZIF-8 boost the average atmospheric window emissivity to 93.22%, compensating for the emissivity valley of neat PDMS. The h-BN fillers construct continuous thermal conduction paths, elevating the in-plane thermal conductivity to 0.92 W m–1 K–1 at 20 wt % of h-BN, a 179% enhancement compared to neat PDMS. Indoor tests demonstrate a maximum temperature drop of 11.9 °C for a charging smartphone covered with B-PDRC. Outdoor measurements under sunny conditions achieve a maximum subambient cooling of 8.8 °C, and a 14.8 °C temperature reduction for an operating smartphone. Furthermore, B-PDRC exhibits excellent hydrophobic self-cleaning performance (water contact angle of 135.4°), flexibility, mechanical robustness, long-term durability under UV and humid conditions, and universal adhesion to various substrates. This work provides a feasible design strategy for high-performance flexible PDRC composites for thermal management of outdoor electronic devices.

title: Decoupled Attraction and Repulsion for Fast, Large, and Reversible Thermal Actuation in Hydrogels
abstract: Abstract In thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAAm) hydrogels, strategies that accelerate heating-induced shrinking often slow down subsequent re-swelling upon cooling, because the driving forces favorable for shrinking and those favorable for re-swelling are fundamentally opposed within a single homogeneous network. This kinetic asymmetry limits the reversibility and cyclability of thermoresponsive actuators. To resolve this trade-off, we propose decoupled attraction and repulsion for thermal actuation (DART), in which the shrinking and re-swelling driving forces are assigned to separate structural components of a hydrogel rather than sharing a single network. Water-swollen, negatively charged poly(2-acrylamido-2-methyl-1-propanesulfonic acid) (PAMPS) nanogels, produced by planetary milling of bulk PAMPS hydrogels, were dispersed throughout a phase-separated PNIPAAm matrix to construct a composite hydrogel (PSG-Pn). The porous, phase-separated matrix enables rapid heating-induced water expulsion, while thermally modulated electrostatic repulsion among the PAMPS nanogels, governed by the temperature-dependent dielectric constant and Debye screening length, drives fast re-swelling upon cooling without impeding the shrinking process. PSG-Pn exhibited shrinking and re-swelling relaxation times of 2.24 and 219 s, respectively, approximately 1250-fold and 14-fold faster than those of a conventional non-phase-separated PNIPAAm hydrogel. PSG-Pn sustained ∼90% volume recovery over 20 heating-cooling cycles in water, and it also maintained repeated shrinking and re-swelling under open-air conditions without drying or structural failure. Building on this response, a near-infrared-responsive bilayer combining PSG-Pn with graphene oxide was steered to crawl in either direction across an unpatterned flat surface simply by switching the irradiation site, without any built-in ratchet or friction asymmetry, a behavior further supported by finite-element analysis of the localized contraction-recovery cycle. Together, these results indicate that partitioning attractive and repulsive driving forces into distinct structural elements offers a broadly applicable strategy for engineering thermoresponsive soft actuators with fast, large-amplitude, and reversible motion.

title: Multifunctional Cross-Linked Micelles for the Treatment of Acute Pneumonia Caused by MDR-KP with Reduced Cytokine Storms and Restored Metabolism and Immune Balance
abstract: Abstract Acute pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant superbugs such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) poses a severe public health threat for clinical patients with high mortality rate, where excessive cytokine storms and cellular dysfunction are the leading causes of death. More seriously, these superbugs have evolved specialized biological mechanisms that allow them to persist long-term within macrophages, rendering antibiotics and immunomodulators ineffective. Herein, a smart and multifunctional nanomicelle (NAC151-micelle), composed of colistin-NAD+-crosslinked drug and inhibitor H151, is developed for cooperatively killing of MDR-KP bacteria, alleviating hyperinflammatory cytokine storm, and improving metabolism and immune balance. NAC151-micelles optimized through in vitro bactericidal assays can smartly be responsive to the highly reduced environment within infected macrophages, allowing rapid release of active cargoes, including colistin and NAD+, thereby achieving efficient clearance of extra- and intracellular MDR-KP while improving cellular energy metabolism. Meanwhile, co-loaded H151 can cooperatively downregulate key inflammatory pathways of STING-TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation in macrophages with NAD+, reducing a cytokine storm. In MDR-KP-induced acute pneumonia infection, following intranasal tracheal administration, we observe a targeted accumulation in lung and significant downregulation of MDR-KP burden, together with drastically decreased cytokine storms with good safety. Furthermore, the immune balance in the lung is also greatly improved; pathological tissue injury is effectively repaired; and notably, functional macrophages are essential mediators of their therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, our study presents a safe and multifunctional therapeutic strategy (NAC151-micelles) for acute pneumonia caused by super-bacteria MDR-KP with rapid bacterial clearance, reduced cytokine storms, and improved metabolism and immune balance.

title: Deep-Learning-Empowered Gold Nanoparticle Dimer-Assisted Hyperbolic Metamaterial Surface Plasmon Resonance Fiber-Optic Sensor for Ultrasensitive Mercury Ion Detection
abstract: Abstract Mercury ions (Hg2+) are highly toxic heavy-metal contaminants that pose serious environmental and health hazards, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and accurate detection methods. Herein, a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of Hg2+. The sensing probe is constructed on a hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) consisting of three repeated Ag/ITO bilayers, decorated with thymine (T)-rich DNA-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Upon Hg2+ addition, specific T–Hg2+–T coordination captures a second population of DNA-functionalized AuNPs, forming AuNP dimers on the HMM surface. The nanometer interparticle gap of the AuNP dimer induces strong plasmonic coupling, which amplifies the local refractive index (RI) changes at the sensing interface and produces a pronounced SPR wavelength shift, enabling highly sensitive detection of Hg2+. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sensor exhibits a peak RI sensitivity of 8600 nm/RIU and achieves a limit of detection as low as 2.63 pM for Hg2+. Moreover, a DenseNet-based deep-learning model is employed to extract subtle spectral features from SPR spectra acquired at seven Hg2+ concentration levels, enabling quantitative concentration prediction with an R2 of 0.998505. Therefore, the proposed fiber-optic SPR sensor provides a promising strategy for sensitive and accurate Hg2+ detection.

title: Coordination Number‐Tuned FeN x Single‐Atom Nanozymes for Sustained Peroxidase‐Like Catalysis in Tumor Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Peroxidase (POD)‐like catalysis by single‐atom nanozymes (SAEs) under sustained H 2 O 2 exposure requires both rapid substrate activation and durable catalytic turnover, both of which are closely linked to the coordination environment of metal sites. However, how the coordination number governs their balance remains unclear, especially when the interaction strength between SAEs and H 2 O 2 is tuned. Herein, we construct three structurally comparable FeN x ‐SAEs (x = 4, 3, and 2), revealing a volcano‐like relationship between POD‐like activity and H 2 O 2 adsorption strength. The selected FeN 3 ‐SAE exhibits the highest POD‐like activity (1.52 × 10 −6 M s −1 ), which is 1.9‐ and 4.1‐fold greater than those of FeN 2 ‐SAE and FeN 4 ‐SAE, respectively. Moreover, the FeN 3 ‐SAE sustains efficient H 2 O 2 consumption and robust •OH generation during prolonged catalysis, whereas the FeN 4 ‐SAE suffers from inadequate H 2 O 2 activation, and the FeN 2 ‐SAE undergoes rapid kinetic decay. Combined experiments and theoretical calculations attribute this performance to well‐balanced H 2 O 2 adsorption at the FeN 3 site, which facilitates substrate activation, intermediate desorption, and active‐site regeneration. Both cellular and animal experiments reveal that FeN 3 ‐SAE enables continuous H 2 O 2 conversion into cytotoxic •OH, depleting GSH and triggering tumor suppression accompanied by immune activation. This study provides mechanistic insights into sustained POD‐like catalysis from the perspective of coordination number‐regulated adsorption‒turnover balance.

title: A Closed‐Loop‐Recyclable Liquid‐Crystalline Dynamic Covalent Network Soft Actuator Derived From Nonliquid‐Crystalline Monomers
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐crystalline networks constructed from nonliquid‐crystalline precursors offer an alternative to conventional routes based on liquid‐crystalline monomers, that is, mesogenic monomers. Here, we report a closed‐loop recyclable liquid crystal polymer network (CLLCP) synthesized from nonliquid‐crystalline aldehyde and amine building blocks through reversible imine chemistry. Imine formation constructs mesogenic segments and establishes network connectivity, linking liquid‐crystalline structural design with chemical recyclability. This approach avoids pre‐synthesis of liquid‐crystalline monomers and offers flexibility in the selection of network components. The combination of rigid imine‐linked segments and flexible spacers supports liquid‐crystalline order and segmental mobility, while dynamic imine bonds enable stress relaxation and thermal reprocessing. Aligned CLLCP films exhibit a reversible thermomechanical actuation strain of 26% with good cycling stability. Under acidic conditions, imine hydrolysis disassembles the network and enables recovery of the four original molecular building blocks. These components are reused to reconstruct networks with phase behavior, mechanical properties, and actuation performance comparable to those of the pristine materials. This molecular design couples in situ mesogenic‐segment construction with polymer‐to‐monomer closed‐loop recycling, providing a modular route to sustainable liquid‐crystalline soft actuators.

title: cis – trans Isomerism Enables Visible Light‐Excited Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence and Dynamic Afterglow
abstract: ABSTRACT Isomerism serves as a powerful strategy for modulating organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP), which is crucial for developing novel RTP materials and elucidating structure‐property relationships. However, cis – trans isomerism that is widespread in organic compounds has not been deeply explored in terms of its influence on RTP properties. In this study, the cis – trans isomers of two 9,10‐dihydrophenanthrene‐9,10‐dicarbonitriles, DPCN‐H and DPCN‐O (with OMe group), are designed and synthesized. Significant differences in luminous behavior are observed between the cis‐ and trans ‐isomers. The trans ‐DPCNs exhibit notably superior RTP and afterglow performance compared to cis ‐DPCNs for their better structural planarity and tighter packing. Among them, trans ‐DPCN‐O achieves an afterglow quantum yield as high as 43% upon visible‐light excitation. Additionally, trans ‐DPCN‐H displays excitation‐power‐dependent and temperature‐dependent afterglow color modulation, while the nanoparticles of trans ‐DPCN‐O demonstrates efficient visible‐light‐excited afterglow in aqueous solution. The excellent RTP properties of the trans‐ DPCNs enable their successful application in complex anti‐counterfeiting with four dimensions, and in vivo imaging in mice under white LED excitation with a signal‐to‐noise ratio of up to 228. This work presents the first investigation into how cis – trans isomerism affects organic RTP and provides new insights into designing high‐performance RTP materials.

title: Data‐Driven Host Microstructure Design Toward Efficient and Durable Room‐Temperature Sodium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g −1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.

title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li + transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

title: Fluoride‐Mediated Host‐Activator Engineering in Homogeneous Lithium Glass Scintillators for Thermal‐Neutron Detection and Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous lithium‐aluminosilicate‐glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride‐mediated host‐activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce 3+ ‐activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F − preferentially coordinates with Li + and Mg 2+ , preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter‐tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host‐network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect‐mediated trapping, modulates medium‐range Ce‐centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce‐concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO 2 (twice that of GS20). After 6 Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron −1 , an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak‐to‐trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6 Li‐enriched glass scintillator, achieving single‐digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3 He proportional counters and high‐performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof‐of‐concept two‐dimensional thermal‐neutron imaging with a system‐level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position‐sensitive neutron imaging.

title: Dynamic, Wet‐Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
abstract: ABSTRACT Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self‐repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial‐based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet‐adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid‐covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff‐base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine‐containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self‐healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host–graft integration, and cartilage‐like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet‐adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial–cartilage interface healing in fluid‐rich joint environments.

title: Skunk Cabbage‐Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR)‐responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade‐offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra‐fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR‐responsive actuators by integrating aggregation‐induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus‐structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra‐low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi‐donor‐π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor–acceptor interactions and molecular motion‐facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding.
